sentences.zh: ◎列傳第三十六　　郭二張三王蘇薛程唐

translations.literal: ◎ Biography 36: Guo, two Zhangs, three Wangs, Su, Xue, Cheng, Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 36: Guo Xiaoke, two members of the Zhang family, three Wangs, Su Dingfang, Xue Rengui, Cheng Mingzhen, and Tang Xiujing.

sentences.zh: =郭孝恪=

translations.literal: = Guo Xiaoke =
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoke

sentences.zh: 郭孝恪，許州陽翟人。

translations.literal: Guo Xiaoke was a native of Yangzhai in Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoke was from Yangzhai in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少有奇節，不治貲產，父兄以爲無賴。

translations.literal: In youth he had unusual resolve; he did not manage family property, and his father and elder brothers regarded him as a wastrel.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he showed uncommon spirit and paid no heed to the family estate; his father and brothers took him for a good-for-nothing.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，率少年數百附李密。

translations.literal: When the Sui order collapsed, he led several hundred youths to join Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil at the end of the Sui, he gathered several hundred young men and attached himself to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密喜，謂曰：「世言汝、潁多奇士，不謬也。

translations.literal: Li Mi was pleased and said to him, "The world says Ru and Ying produce many extraordinary men—this is no empty claim.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was delighted and told him, "People say the Ru and Ying region breeds remarkable men, and they are not wrong.

sentences.zh: 」使與李勣守黎陽。

translations.literal: " He had him guard Liyang together with Li Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " He assigned him, together with Li Ji, to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 密敗，勣遣孝恪送款，封陽翟郡公，拜宋州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Mi was defeated, Li Ji sent Xiaoke to offer allegiance; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangzhai Commandery and appointed prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat, Li Ji sent Xiaoke to submit to the Tang court; he was created Duke of Yangzhai and made prefect of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔與勣經略武牢以東，所定州縣，委以選補。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him, with Li Ji, to pacify the region east of Wulao; for the prefectures and counties they secured, he was entrusted with selecting and filling offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to campaign with Li Ji east of Wulao, and for every prefecture and county they brought under control he was given authority to appoint officials.

sentences.zh: 竇建德之援洛也，孝恪上謁秦王，進計曰：「王世充力竭計窮，其面縛可跂足待。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande came to relieve Luoyang, Xiaoke went up to the Prince of Qin and offered a plan, saying, "Wang Shichong's strength is spent and his stratagems exhausted; his being bound and delivered can be awaited at a leisurely pace.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande marched to relieve Luoyang, Xiaoke presented himself to the Prince of Qin and advised, "Wang Shichong is at the end of his strength and his wits; we can wait at our ease for him to be brought in with hands bound.

sentences.zh: 建德悉眾遠來，糧餉阻絶，殆天亡時也。

translations.literal: Jiande has led all his forces from afar; their grain and supplies are cut off—this is almost the hour Heaven decrees their fall.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande has marched his entire army from far away with his supply lines severed; Heaven itself seems ready to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 若固守武牢，以軍汜水，逐機應變，擒殄必矣！

translations.literal: If we hold fast at Wulao and station troops at Sishui, adapting to opportunity as it arises, capture and annihilation are certain!
translations.idiomatic: If we stand firm at Wulao and post our army at Sishui, responding to each turn of events, we are sure to take and destroy him!

sentences.zh: 」王然之。

translations.literal: " The prince approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊平，置酒大會洛陽宮，語諸將曰：「孝恪策擒賊，王長先下漕，功固在諸君右。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he set out wine for a great assembly in the Luoyang palace and told the generals, "Xiaoke's plan captured the enemy; Wang Chang was first to descend the canal—his merit surely stands above you all.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, he held a grand banquet in the Luoyang palace and told his generals, "It was Xiaoke's strategy that brought the enemy down, and Wang Chang was first on the canal route—his achievement is plainly above yours.

sentences.zh: 」遷上柱國。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to the rank of Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 歷貝、趙、江、涇四州刺史，所至有能名。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Bei, Zhao, Jiang, and Jing prefectures; wherever he went he won a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Bei, Zhao, Jiang, and Jing, and everywhere he went he earned a name for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 改左驍衛將軍，累加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and repeatedly advanced to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and rose by stages to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年，拜涼州都督，改安西都護、西州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan he was appointed military governor of Liangzhou, then made Protector-General of the Pacified West and prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 642 he was named military governor of Liangzhou, then Protector-General of the Pacified West and prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 其地高昌舊都，流徙罪人與鎮兵雜，限以沙磧，隔絶中國，孝恪推誠撫禦，盡得其歡心。

translations.literal: The place was the old capital of Gaochang; transported convicts were mixed with garrison troops, bounded by sandy wastes and cut off from China. Xiaoke treated them with sincerity and governed them gently, winning all their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The region was the former capital of Gaochang, where exiled convicts lived among frontier garrisons, separated from the heartland by desert wastes. Xiaoke ruled with open sincerity and kindness and won the people's complete trust.

sentences.zh: 初，王師滅高昌，詔以所虜焉耆生口七百還焉耆王。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the imperial army destroyed Gaochang, an edict ordered that seven hundred Kuchean captives taken be returned to the king of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces had earlier destroyed Gaochang, the court had ordered seven hundred Kuchean captives to be returned to the king of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 王叛歸欲谷設可汗，孝恪請擊之，即拜西州道行軍總管，率步騎三千出銀山道，夜襲其王龍突騎支，虜之。

translations.literal: The king rebelled and went over to the Yehu She Khan; Xiaoke requested an attack, was at once appointed commander on campaign of the Xizhou route, led three thousand infantry and cavalry out by the Yinshan road, and by night raided the king Long Tuqizhi and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The king rebelled and fled to the Yehu She Khan. Xiaoke asked leave to strike him, was immediately made commander on the Xizhou campaign route, led three thousand foot and horse out along the Yinshan road, and in a night assault seized King Long Tuqizhi.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，降璽書褒勞。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and sent down an imperial letter of praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and sent a sealed edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 俄拜昆丘道副大總管，進討龜茲，破其國城，乃自留守，遣餘軍分道進。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed deputy supreme commander on the Kunqiu route and advanced to attack Kucha; he breached the state capital, then himself remained on guard and sent the remaining armies forward by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made deputy supreme commander on the Kunqiu route and marched against Kucha. After breaking the capital he stayed behind as garrison commander while the rest of the army advanced along several routes.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國相那利遁去。

translations.literal: Nali, chief minister of Kucha, fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Nali, the Kuchean chief minister, had escaped.

sentences.zh: 孝恪以餘部未平，出營於外。

translations.literal: Xiaoke, because the remaining bands were not yet pacified, went out to camp beyond the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Because the remaining enemy forces were not yet subdued, Xiaoke moved his camp outside the city.

sentences.zh: 國人有謂孝恪曰：「那利素得士心，今亡在外，勢必爲變，城中頗有異志，願公備之。

translations.literal: A man of the state said to Xiaoke, "Nali has long held the hearts of the soldiers; now that he is at large outside, he is sure to stir up trouble, and there are many in the city with contrary intent—my lord, please take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: A local man warned Xiaoke, "Nali has always commanded the loyalty of the troops. Now that he is free outside the walls he is certain to make trouble, and many inside the city are of doubtful mind. I beg you to be on your guard.

sentences.zh: 」孝恪忽其言，不設備。

translations.literal: " Xiaoke disregarded his words and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaoke ignored the warning and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 那利果率眾陰與城內胡爲應，薄城鼓噪，始覺之，乃率千餘人合戰，城中舉應那利，孝恪殊死鬥，中流矢卒，子待詔亦歿。

translations.literal: Nali indeed led his forces in secret coordination with the Hu inside the city; they pressed the walls with drums and shouts. Only then did Xiaoke realize it. He then led somewhat more than a thousand men to join battle; the city rose in response to Nali. Xiaoke fought to the death, was struck by a flying arrow and died, and his son Daizhao also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Nali did in fact rally his men and secretly coordinated with the non-Chinese inside the city. They stormed the walls with drums and clamor before Xiaoke understood what was happening. He led a little over a thousand men into a desperate fight while the city rose for Nali. Xiaoke battled to the last and was killed by an arrow; his son Daizhao died as well.

sentences.zh: 將軍曹繼叔進兵，復拔其城。

translations.literal: General Cao Jishu advanced his troops and again took the city.
translations.idiomatic: General Cao Jishu marched up and recaptured the city.

sentences.zh: 太宗責孝恪斥候不明，至顛覆，奪其官。

translations.literal: Taizong blamed Xiaoke for unclear scouting that led to overturning defeat and stripped him of his offices.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong held Xiaoke responsible for poor intelligence that had led to disaster and posthumously stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 後湣死戰，更爲舉哀。

translations.literal: Later, pitying his death in battle, he again ordered mourning rites performed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, moved by pity for his death in battle, the emperor ordered mourning rites held for him again.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追還官爵，贈待詔遊擊將軍，賻物三百段。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he restored his offices and titles posthumously, granted Daizhao the posthumous title of General on Campaign of the Palace Attendant, and gave three hundred rolls of funerary goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne he restored Xiaoke's offices and titles, posthumously made Daizhao General on Campaign of the Palace Attendant, and granted three hundred rolls of burial goods.

sentences.zh: 次子待封，官左豹韜衛將軍。

translations.literal: The second son, Daifeng, held office as general of the Left Leopard Bow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Daifeng served as general of the Left Leopard Bow Guard.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，副薛仁貴討吐番，戰大非川，敗績，貸死爲民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng he served as deputy to Xue Rengui in campaigning against the Tibetans; they fought at Dafeichuan, suffered defeat, and his death sentence was commuted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianheng era he served under Xue Rengui against the Tibetans, was defeated at the battle of Dafeichuan, and was spared execution only to be reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: =張儉=

translations.literal: = Zhang Jian =
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian

sentences.zh: 張儉，字師約，京兆新豐人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, courtesy name Shiyue, was a native of Xinfeng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, styled Shiyue, was from Xinfeng in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 隋相州刺史、皖城郡公威孫。

translations.literal: He was grandson of Wei, Sui prefect of Xiangzhou and Duke of Wancheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Wei, who had been Sui prefect of Xiangzhou and Duke of Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 父植，車騎將軍、連城縣公。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Liancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Liancheng.

sentences.zh: 儉，高祖從外孫也。

translations.literal: Jian was a maternal grandson of Gaozu's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a maternal grandson of a cousin of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖起，儉以功除右衛郎將，遷朔州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose, Jian was appointed Right Guard Commandant for merit and was transferred to prefect of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his banner, Jian was made Right Guard commandant for his service and later became prefect of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 時頡利可汗方強，每有求取，所遣書輒稱詔敕，邊吏奉承不敢卻。

translations.literal: At that time the Khan Jieli was still powerful; whenever he made demands, the letters he sent invariably styled themselves as imperial edicts, and frontier officials complied and dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Khan Jieli was at the height of his power. Every demand arrived in documents styled as imperial edicts, and border officials obeyed them without daring to refuse.

sentences.zh: 及儉，獨拒不受。

translations.literal: When it came to Jian, he alone refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jian alone refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 大教民營田，歳收谷數十萬斛。

translations.literal: He greatly instructed the people in garrison farming; each year the grain harvest reached several hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: He vigorously promoted military farming among the people, and each year the harvest ran to several hundred thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 雖霜旱，勸百姓相振贍，免饑殍，州以完安。

translations.literal: Even through frost and drought he urged the people to aid one another, averted starvation corpses, and the prefecture remained intact and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Even in years of frost and drought he urged mutual relief among the people, kept starvation at bay, and left the prefecture whole and at peace.

sentences.zh: 李靖既平突厥，有思結部者，窮歸於儉，儉受而安輯之。

translations.literal: After Li Jing had pacified the Turks, a group of the Sinie tribe, driven to extremity, came to Jian; he received them and settled them in peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jing had defeated the Turks, members of the Sinie tribe, brought to ruin, came to Jian, and he received and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 其在磧北者，親戚私相過省，儉不禁，示羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Those who were north of the desert visited kin in private; Jian did not forbid it, merely showing a policy of loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: Those who lived north of the desert crossed back and forth to visit kin; Jian did not stop them, merely signaling a policy of loose control.

sentences.zh: 儉徙勝州，後將不察其然，遽奏思結叛，朝廷議進討，時儉以母喪，奪服爲使者撫納之。

translations.literal: Jian was transferred to Shengzhou. A later commander, not discerning the true situation, hastily memorialized that the Sinie had rebelled; the court debated advancing to attack. At that time Jian was in mourning for his mother but left mourning garb to serve as envoy and soothe and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was transferred to Shengzhou, a later commander, failing to understand the situation, hastily reported that the Sinie had rebelled and the court debated a punitive campaign. Jian was then in mourning for his mother but set mourning aside to go as envoy and win them back.

sentences.zh: 儉單騎入其部，召酋帥慰諭，推腹心，咸匍匐歸命，因舉徙代州，遂檢校代州都督。

translations.literal: Jian entered their territory alone on horseback, summoned the chieftains to comfort and instruct them, opened his inmost heart to them, and all prostrated themselves in submission; he then moved them en masse to Daizhou and was made acting military governor of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian rode alone into their camps, summoned the chiefs, spoke to them with complete frankness, and won them all to submission on their knees. He then moved the whole tribe to Daizhou and was made acting military governor there.

sentences.zh: 儉勸墾田力耕，歳數稔，私蓄富實。

translations.literal: Jian urged opening fields and strenuous cultivation; for several years harvests were abundant and private stores grew rich and full.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the people to open new land and farm diligently. For several years the harvests were rich and private granaries overflowed.

sentences.zh: 儉恐虜易驕，乃建平糴法，入之官，虜悅喜，由是儲斛流贏。

translations.literal: Jian feared the tribes would grow arrogant with ease, so he established a system of leveling purchases: grain went into government stores, the tribes were pleased and delighted, and thereby stored grain flowed in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the tribes would grow arrogant from easy plenty, he instituted a grain-purchase system that channeled surplus into government stores. The tribes were pleased, and government reserves swelled.

sentences.zh: 遷營州都督，兼護東夷校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Yingzhou and concurrently Colonel Protecting the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Yingzhou and concurrently Colonel Protecting the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 坐事免，詔白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense but was ordered to retain his duties in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for an offense but ordered to continue his duties as a commoner in official service.

sentences.zh: 營州部與契丹、奚、霫、靺鞨諸蕃切畛，高麗引眾入寇，儉率兵破之，俘斬略盡。

translations.literal: The Yingzhou district bordered the Khitan, Xi, Hui, Mohe, and other tribes; Goguryeo led forces in invasion, and Jian led troops to defeat them, capturing and beheading nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou lay cheek by jowl with the Khitan, Xi, Hui, Mohe, and other frontier peoples. When Goguryeo invaded with a large force, Jian met them in battle and all but annihilated them, taking captives and heads in great number.

sentences.zh: 復拜營州都督。

translations.literal: He was again appointed military governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed military governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗將征遼東，遣儉率蕃兵先進，略地至遼西，川漲，久未度。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign against Liaodong, he sent Jian to lead tribal troops in advance to seize territory as far as Liaoxi; the rivers swelled and for a long time they could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to campaign against Liaodong he sent Jian ahead with tribal auxiliaries to seize ground as far as western Liaodong, but flooded rivers long kept the army from crossing.

sentences.zh: 帝以爲畏懦，召還。

translations.literal: The emperor thought him timid and cowardly and recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this for cowardice and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 見洛陽宮，陳水草美惡、山川險易，並久不進狀。

translations.literal: When he was received at the Luoyang palace, he set forth the good and bad of pastures and waters, the difficult and easy of mountains and rivers, and the long delay in advancing—all in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Received at the Luoyang palace, he explained in a memorial the quality of pastures and waterways, the lay of the land, and why the advance had taken so long.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，拜行軍總管，使領諸蕃騎，爲六軍前鋒。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, appointed him commander on campaign, and had him lead all tribal cavalry as vanguard of the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, made him commander on campaign, and set him at the head of all tribal cavalry as vanguard of the six armies.

sentences.zh: 時高麗候者言莫離支且至，帝詔儉自新城路邀擊，虜不敢出。

translations.literal: At that time Goguryeo scouts said Yeon Gaesomun was about to arrive; the emperor ordered Jian to intercept him by the Xincheng route, and the enemy dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo scouts reported that Yeon Gaesomun was approaching, the emperor ordered Jian to ambush him on the Xincheng road, and the enemy did not dare show themselves.

sentences.zh: 儉進度遼，趨建安城，破賊，斬數千級。

translations.literal: Jian advanced, crossed the Liao, hastened to Jian'an city, defeated the rebels, and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jian crossed the Liao, pushed on to Jian'an, routed the enemy, and took several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 累封皖城郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 後改東夷校尉官爲都護府，即以儉爲都護。

translations.literal: Later the office of Colonel of the Eastern Yi was changed to a Protectorate, and Jian was made protector.
translations.idiomatic: Later the office of Colonel of the Eastern Yi was converted into a protectorate, and Jian was made its protector.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he was advanced to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui era he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十，謚曰密。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty; his posthumous title was Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty and was given the posthumous name Mi.

sentences.zh: 儉兄大師，太僕卿、華州刺史、武功縣男。

translations.literal: Jian's elder brother Dash, was Minister of the Imperial Stud, prefect of Huazhou, and Baron of Wugong County.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's elder brother Dash was Minister of the Imperial Stud, prefect of Hua, and Baron of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 弟延師，左衛大將軍、范陽郡公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanshi was General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Duke of Fanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanshi was General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 性謹畏，黃羽林兵三十年，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: His nature was cautious and reverent; for thirty years in the Yellow Feather Forest guard he never once had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious by nature and served thirty years in the Feathered Forest guard without a single blemish on his record.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈荊州都督，謚曰敬，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made military governor of Jingzhou, given the posthumous title Jing, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made military governor of Jingzhou, given the posthumous name Jing, and buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 儉兄弟三人門皆立戟，時號「三戟張家」。

translations.literal: All three brothers of the Zhang family had halberds set up at their gates; at the time they were called "the Zhang family of three halberds."
translations.idiomatic: All three Zhang brothers kept ceremonial halberds at their gates, and people called them "the house of three halberds."

sentences.zh: =王方翼=

translations.literal: = Wang Fangyi =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangyi

sentences.zh: 王方翼，字仲翔，并州祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Fangyi, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a native of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangyi, styled Zhongxiang, was from Qi in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖裕，隨州刺史，尚同安大長公主，官開府儀同三司，卒，謚曰文。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was prefect of Suizhou, married the Princess of Tong'an the Greater, held the office of Grand Master with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Dukes, died, and was given the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu was prefect of Suizhou, married the Princess of Tong'an the Greater, rose to the rank of Grand Master with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Dukes, and after his death received the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 方翼早孤，哀毀如成人，時號孝童。

translations.literal: Fangyi was orphaned early; in grief and self-injury he was like an adult, and at the time he was called the Filial Child.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi lost his father early and mourned with the gravity of a grown man; people called him the Filial Child.

sentences.zh: 母李，爲主所斥，居鳳泉墅。

translations.literal: His mother, of the Li clan, was expelled by the princess and lived at the Fengquan estate.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Li, had been cast out by the princess and lived at the Fengquan villa.

sentences.zh: 方翼尚幼，雜庸保，執苦不棄日，墾田植樹，治林垠，既完墻屋，燎松丸墨，爲富家。

translations.literal: Fangyi was still young; he mingled with hired laborers and bondservants, endured hardship without resting by day, opened fields and planted trees, tended the forest margins, completed walls and houses, burned pine for ink pellets, and became a wealthy household.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, Fangyi worked alongside hired hands and bondservants, toiling every day without rest. He cleared fields, planted trees, tended the woods, rebuilt the walls and roofs, even made ink from pine soot, and turned the household into a prosperous one.

sentences.zh: 主薨，還京師。

translations.literal: When the princess died, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess died he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜行，見長人丈餘，引弓射仆之，乃配木也。

translations.literal: Once on a night journey he saw a tall man of more than ten feet, drew his bow and shot him down—but it was only a wooden post.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a night walk he saw a figure more than ten feet tall, drew his bow and felled it, only to find it was a wooden post.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞，擢右千牛。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it, he promoted him to Right Thousand-Ox.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard the story he appointed him to the Right Thousand-Ox guard.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，而從祖女弟爲皇后，調安定令，誅滅大姓，奸豪脅息。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, a female cousin on his father's side became empress; Fangyi was transferred to magistrate of Anding, executed and destroyed the great clans, and the powerful ruffians were cowed into silence.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne a cousin on his father's side became empress. Fangyi was made magistrate of Anding, where he broke the great clans and cowed the local bullies into silence.

sentences.zh: 徙瀚海都護司馬，坐事下遷朔州尚德府果毅，歳餘代還。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be marshal of the Hanhai Protectorate; for an offense he was demoted to captain of the Guoyi company in Shangde Prefecture, Shuozhou, and after somewhat more than a year was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be marshal of the Hanhai Protectorate, then demoted for an offense to captain of a company in Shangde, Shuozhou. After a little more than a year he was relieved and recalled.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，哀瘠甚，帝遣侍醫療視。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother he was emaciated with grief to an extreme degree; the emperor sent palace physicians to treat and observe him.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he grew dangerously thin with grief, and the emperor sent court physicians to care for him.

sentences.zh: 其友趙持滿誅死，屍諸道，親戚莫敢視，方翼曰：「欒布哭彭越，義也；

translations.literal: His friend Zhao Chiman was executed by decapitation; his corpse was displayed along the road and kin dared not look upon it. Fangyi said, "Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue—that was righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: His friend Zhao Chiman was executed and his body left on the road; none of his kin dared approach. Fangyi said, "When Luan Bu mourned Peng Yue he acted in the name of righteousness;

sentences.zh: 周文王掩骼，仁也。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou covered exposed bones—that was benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: when King Wen of Zhou buried the unburied dead he acted in the name of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 絶友義，蔽主仁，何以事君？

translations.literal: To cut off friendship's righteousness and obscure a ruler's benevolence—how may one then serve a lord?
translations.idiomatic: If one cuts off the righteousness owed a friend and hides a ruler's benevolence, how can one serve one's lord?

sentences.zh: 」遂往哭其屍，具禮收葬。

translations.literal: " He then went to weep over the corpse and, with full rites, gathered and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to weep over the body and buried it with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 金吾劾繫，帝嘉之，不罪。

translations.literal: The Golden Crow arrested and imprisoned him; the emperor praised him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Crow guard arrested him, but the emperor commended him and imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 再遷肅州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 州無隍塹，寇易以攻，方翼乃發卒建樓堞，廝多樂水自環，烽邏精明。

translations.literal: The prefecture had no moat or rampart and bandits could attack with ease; Fangyi then raised troops to build towers and battlements, had the laborers channel the Duoled River to encircle the city, and made beacon and patrol arrangements keen and clear.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had no walls or moat and was easy prey for raiders. Fangyi drafted laborers to build towers and battlements, diverted the Duoled River to ring the city, and organized beacons and patrols with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳間，河西蝗，獨不至方翼境，而它郡民或餒死，皆重繭走方翼治下。

translations.literal: During the Yifeng era locusts struck Hexi, but alone did not reach Fangyi's territory; in other prefectures people sometimes starved to death, and all came swaddled in layers of rags to live under Fangyi's rule.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era locusts ravaged the Hexi region but did not touch Fangyi's jurisdiction. In neighboring prefectures people starved, and refugees in ragged layers of clothing flocked to his domain.

sentences.zh: 乃出私錢作水硙，簿其贏，以濟饑瘵，構舍數十百楹居之，全活甚眾，芝產其地。

translations.literal: He then spent private funds to build water mills, kept accounts of their profit, used it to relieve hunger and pestilence, erected dwellings of several tens and hundreds of bays to house them, saved and kept alive very many, and auspicious fungus appeared in his territory.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his own money to build water mills, recorded their profits, and used the proceeds to relieve famine and disease. He put up hundreds of rooms to shelter the destitute and saved a great multitude; miraculous fungus even appeared in his territory.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉討遮匐，奏爲副，兼檢校安西都護，徙故都護杜懷寶爲庭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Pei Xingjian campaigned against Zhefu, he memorialized for Fangyi as deputy and concurrently acting Protector-General of the Pacified West, transferring the former protector Du Huaibao to prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Xingjian campaigned against Zhefu he asked for Fangyi as his deputy and acting Protector-General of the Pacified West, while the former protector Du Huaibao was moved to prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 方翼築碎葉城，面三門，紆還多趣以詭出入，五旬畢。

translations.literal: Fangyi built Suyab city facing three gates, with winding, many-branched approaches to deceive entry and exit; it was completed in fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi built the city of Suyab with three gates and a maze of winding approaches designed to confuse attackers, and finished it in fifty days.

sentences.zh: 西域胡縱觀，莫測其方略，悉獻珍貨。

translations.literal: Western-region Hu came in crowds to look on, could not fathom his strategy, and all presented rare goods.
translations.idiomatic: Western peoples came in crowds to watch and, unable to guess his design, all brought him tribute of rare goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙方翼庭州刺史，而懷寶自金山都護更鎮安西，遂失蕃戎之和。

translations.literal: Before long Fangyi was transferred to prefect of Tingzhou while Huaibao moved from Colonel of the Golden Mountain Protectorate back to garrison the Pacified West, and thereby the harmony of the frontier tribes was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fangyi was moved to Tingzhou while Huaibao was shifted from the Golden Mountain protectorate back to the Pacified West, and harmony with the frontier peoples was lost.

sentences.zh: 永淳初，十姓阿史那車簿啜叛，圍弓月城，方翼引軍戰伊麗河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchun, Chebochuo of the Ashina of the Ten Surnames rebelled and besieged Gongyue city; Fangyi led troops to fight on the Yili River.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongchun era Chebochuo of the Ashina of the Ten Surnames rebelled and besieged Gongyue. Fangyi led his army to battle on the Yili River.

sentences.zh: 敗之，斬首千級。

translations.literal: He defeated them and beheaded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them and took a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 俄而三姓咽面兵十萬踵至，方翼次熱海，進戰，矢著臂，引佩刀斷去，左右莫知。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a hundred thousand troops of the Three Surnames of Yanmian followed hard upon him; Fangyi encamped at the Hot Sea and advanced to battle. An arrow struck his arm; he drew his belt knife and cut it off, and those at his side did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a hundred thousand warriors of the Three Surnames of Yanmian came up behind him. Fangyi made camp at the Hot Sea and gave battle. An arrow struck his arm; he cut it off with his belt knife without those around him noticing.

sentences.zh: 所部雜虜謀執方翼爲內應，方翼悉召會軍中，厚賜，以次出壁外，縛之。

translations.literal: Mixed tribesmen in his command plotted to seize Fangyi as an inside collaborator; Fangyi summoned them all to assemble in camp, richly rewarded them, then had them go out beyond the walls in turn and bound them.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the mixed tribesmen in his command plotted to seize him as a hostage for the enemy. Fangyi summoned them all into camp, lavished gifts on them, then had them led out beyond the walls one by one and bound.

sentences.zh: 會大風，雜金鼓，而號呼無聞者，殺七千人。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind arose; he mingled gongs and drums with it, and amid shouts and cries none could be heard; he killed seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind arose just then. He mingled the clash of gongs and drums with the storm so that his men's cries could not be heard, and put seven thousand to death.

sentences.zh: 即遣騎分道襲咽面等，皆驚潰，烏鶻引兵遁去，擒首領突騎施等三百人，西戎震服。

translations.literal: He then sent cavalry by separate routes to strike Yanmian and others; all were startled and routed. Wugu led his troops in flight, and chieftains including Turgesh and others, three hundred men, were captured; the western tribes were shaken into submission.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent cavalry along separate routes against the Yanmian and others, who broke in panic. Wugu fled with his army, and three hundred chieftains including those of the Turgesh were taken. The western peoples submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 初，方翼次葛水，暴漲，師不可度，沈祭以禱，師涉而濟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fangyi had encamped at the Ge River, it rose in sudden flood and the army could not cross; he cast offerings into the water to pray, and the army waded across and reached the other bank.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fangyi halted at the Ge River, a sudden flood made crossing impossible. He cast offerings into the water in prayer, and the army forded the river and reached the far bank.

sentences.zh: 又七月次葉河，無舟，而冰一昔合。

translations.literal: Again, in the seventh month he halted at the Ye River; there were no boats, yet in one night the ice joined solid.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he camped at the Ye River without boats, yet overnight the ice formed a solid bridge.

sentences.zh: 時以爲祥。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: People took this as a sign of Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 西域平，以功遷夏州都督。

translations.literal: When the Western Regions were pacified, for his merit he was transferred to military governor of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Western Regions were pacified he was promoted to military governor of Xia Prefecture for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 屬牛疫，民廢田作，方翼爲耦耕法，張機鍵，力省而見功多，百姓順賴。

translations.literal: There happened to be a cattle plague; the people abandoned field work. Fangyi devised a paired-plow method, set up mechanical linkages, saved labor yet achieved much work, and the common people relied on him in compliance.
translations.idiomatic: When a cattle plague left the fields untilled, Fangyi introduced paired-plow farming with mechanical rigging that saved labor while increasing yield, and the people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 明年，召方翼議西域事，引見奉天宮，賜食帝前，帝見衣有汙濯處，問其故，具對熱海苦戰狀。

translations.literal: The next year Fangyi was summoned to discuss Western Region affairs, was received in audience at Fengtian Palace, and was granted food before the emperor. The emperor saw stained and washed places on his clothes, asked the reason, and he fully recounted the bitter fighting at the Hot Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Fangyi was summoned to discuss affairs in the west and received at Fengtian Palace, where the emperor fed him at table. Seeing stains on his robes, the emperor asked the cause, and Fangyi told in full of the hard fighting at the Hot Sea.

sentences.zh: 視其創，帝咨嗟久之，賜賚良厚。

translations.literal: When the emperor looked at his wounds, he sighed in admiration for a long time and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor examined his wounds, sighed long in admiration, and gave him lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 俄而妖賊白鐵餘以綏州反，詔方翼與程務挺討之。

translations.literal: Soon the demonic rebel Bai Tieyu rose in rebellion at Suizhou; an edict ordered Fangyi and Cheng Wuting to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebel Bai Tieyu rose at Suizhou, and Fangyi was ordered with Cheng Wuting to put him down.

sentences.zh: 飛■擊賊，火其柵，平之，封太原郡公。

translations.literal: He launched flying stones against the rebels, burned their palisades, pacified them, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He battered the rebels with catapult stones, burned their stockades, and crushed the revolt, for which he was created Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 阿史那元珍入寇，被詔進擊。

translations.literal: Ashina Yuanzhen invaded; he received an edict to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina Yuanzhen invaded he was ordered to take the field against him.

sentences.zh: 時庫無完鎧，方翼斷六板，畫虎文，鉤聯解合，賊馬忽見，奔駭，遂敗，獲大將二，因降桑乾、舍利二部。

translations.literal: At that time the armory had no intact armor; Fangyi cut six boards, painted them with tiger patterns, and linked them with hooks so they could be joined and separated. When the enemy horses suddenly saw them, they bolted in terror; he was thus victorious, captured two great generals, and thereby received the submission of the Sanggan and Sheli tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The armory had no whole suits of armor, so Fangyi cut six boards, painted them with tigers, and hinged them together. Enemy horses took fright at the sight and bolted. He routed the foe, took two senior generals, and won the submission of the Sanggan and Sheli tribes.

sentences.zh: 武后時，王后屬無在者，方翼自視功多，冀不坐，而後內欲因罪除之，未得也。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, none of the Wang clan remained; Fangyi, viewing his many achievements, hoped he would not be implicated, while within the palace the empress wished to remove him through charges but had not yet succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu none of the Wang clan still survived. Fangyi, counting his many services, hoped to escape punishment, while the empress within the palace sought a pretext to destroy him but had not yet found one.

sentences.zh: 及務挺被殺，即並坐方翼，追入朝，捕送獄，流崖州，卒於道，年六十三。

translations.literal: When Wuting was killed, Fangyi was implicated at once, recalled to court, arrested and sent to prison, exiled to Yazhou, and died on the road at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuting was executed Fangyi was implicated, summoned to court, imprisoned, and exiled to Yazhou. He died on the road at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong his offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era his offices and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 方翼善書，與魏叔琬齊名。

translations.literal: Fangyi was skilled at calligraphy and was famed equally with Wei Shuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi was an accomplished calligrapher, ranked with Wei Shuyan.

sentences.zh: 方翼子 珣子珣，字伯玉，與兄璵、弟瑨以文學稱，時號「三王」。

translations.literal: Fangyi's son Xun, courtesy name Boyu, together with his elder brother Yu and younger brother Jin were famed for letters and learning; at the time they were called "the three Wangs."
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi's son Xun, styled Boyu, with his elder brother Yu and younger brother Jin were known for literary talent and were called "the three Wangs."

sentences.zh: 天授初，珣及進士第，應制科，遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou, Xun passed the jinshi examination and the special imperial examination, and was transferred to assistant magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshou era Xun passed the jinshi and special imperial examinations and was made assistant magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 以拔萃擢長安尉，因進見，武后召問刑政，嘉之。

translations.literal: For outstanding selection he was promoted to assistant magistrate of Chang'an; through an audience presentation Empress Wu summoned him to question him on criminal administration and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted for exceptional merit to assistant magistrate of Chang'an, he was presented at court. Empress Wu questioned him on criminal law and commended him.

sentences.zh: 詢其族氏，對曰：「廢後，臣之姑也。

translations.literal: She asked his clan affiliation; he answered, "The deposed empress was my father's sister.
translations.idiomatic: She asked his lineage. He replied, "The deposed empress was my aunt.

sentences.zh: 」後不悅，左遷亳州司法參軍。

translations.literal: " The empress was displeased and demoted him to legal adjutant of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress was displeased and demoted him to legal adjutant at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，爲河南丞，武三思矯制貶臨川令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was vice-prefect of Henan; Wu Sansi forged an edict and demoted him to magistrate of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was vice-prefect of Henan until Wu Sansi forged an edict demoting him to magistrate of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 宋璟輔政，召授侍御史。

translations.literal: When Song Jing assisted in government, he was summoned and appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jing took power he was recalled and made attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 出許州長史。

translations.literal: He went out as chief administrator of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief administrator of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歳旱，珣時假刺史事，開廩振民，即自劾，玄宗赦之。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, Xun was then acting prefect; he opened the granaries to relieve the people, immediately impeached himself, and Xuanzong pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought, while acting prefect he opened the granaries to feed the people, then impeached himself. Xuanzong pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 而瑨至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Jin rose to Attendant Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jin rose to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 珣嘗爲秘書少監，數年而瑨繼職。

translations.literal: Xun once served as Vice Director of the Palace Library; several years later Jin succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had once been vice director of the Palace Library; several years later Jin succeeded him in that office.

sentences.zh: 終右散騎常侍，卒。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and died.

sentences.zh: 贈戸部尚書，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Revenue; his posthumous title was Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Revenue and given the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子鋗，天寶中歷右補闕、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His son Tao, during the Tianbao era successively served as Right Remonstrator and Attendant Censor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao served in the Tianbao era as Right Remonstrator and palace censor.

sentences.zh: 瑨子鉷，自有傳。

translations.literal: Jin's son Hong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Hong has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: =蘇烈=

translations.literal: = Su Lie =
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang

sentences.zh: 蘇烈，字定方，以字行，冀州武邑人，後徙始平。

translations.literal: Su Lie, courtesy name Dingfang, was known by his courtesy name; he was a native of Wuyi in Jizhou and later moved to Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Su Lie, styled Dingfang and known by that name, was from Wuyi in Ji Prefecture and later moved to Shiping.

sentences.zh: 父邕，當隋季，率里中數千人爲本郡討賊。

translations.literal: His father Yong, at the end of the Sui, led several thousand men of the village district to campaign against bandits for the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong, in the closing years of the Sui, led several thousand local men in the commandery's campaigns against bandits.

sentences.zh: 定方驍悍有氣決，年十五，從父戰，數先登陷陣。

translations.literal: Dingfang was fierce and bold with resolute spirit; at age fifteen he followed his father in battle and many times was first to ascend and break the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang was fierce and resolute. At fifteen he fought under his father and many times was first over the wall and into the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 邕卒，代領其眾，破劇賊張金稱、楊公卿，追北數十里，自是賊不舍境，鄕黨賴之。

translations.literal: When Yong died, he succeeded in command of his forces, defeated the fierce bandits Zhang Jincheng and Yang Gongqing, pursued them north for several tens of li, and from then on bandits did not dare leave the borders; the village districts relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong's death he took command, defeated the major bandits Zhang Jincheng and Yang Gongqing, and pursued them north for miles. From then on bandits did not dare cross the border, and the countryside owed him its safety.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，爲匡道府折衝，從李靖襲突厥頡利於磧口，率彀馬二百爲前鋒，乘霧行，去賊一里許，霧霽，見牙帳，馳殺數十百人，頡利及隋公主惶窘各遁去，靖亦尋至，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was Colonel of the Kuangdao Garrison; he followed Li Jing in raiding the Turk Jieli at Qikou, led two hundred armored horses as vanguard, marched through fog, and when about a li from the enemy the fog cleared and he saw the royal tent; he galloped in and killed several tens and hundreds of men. Jieli and the Sui princess fled in panic each their own way; Jing also soon arrived, and the remaining followers all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was a garrison colonel at Kuangdao and followed Li Jing's raid on the Turk khan Jieli at Qikou. Leading two hundred armored horsemen as vanguard through the fog, he emerged a li from the enemy camp, saw the royal tent, and charged, killing hundreds. Jieli and the Sui princess fled in panic. Li Jing arrived soon after and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 再遷左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Commandant of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to commandant of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 與程名振討高麗，破之。

translations.literal: With Cheng Mingzhen he campaigned against Goguryeo and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Goguryeo with Cheng Mingzhen and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 拜右屯衛將軍、臨清縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Garrison Guard and Duke of Linqing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the Right Garrison Guard and Duke of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 從蔥山道大總管程知節征賀魯，至鷹娑川，賀魯率二萬騎來拒，總管蘇海政連戰未決，鼠尼施等復引二萬騎爲援。

translations.literal: He followed the Congshan-route supreme commander Cheng Zhijie in campaigning against Helu; they reached the Yingsuo River. Helu led twenty thousand cavalry to resist; the commander Su Haizheng fought repeatedly without decision, and Shunishi and others again led twenty thousand cavalry as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: He followed supreme commander Cheng Zhijie on the Congshan route against Helu. At the Yingsuo River, Helu met them with twenty thousand horsemen. Su Haizheng fought repeated engagements without a clear outcome while Shunishi brought another twenty thousand horsemen in support.

sentences.zh: 定方始休士，見塵起，率精騎五百，逾嶺馳搗賊營，賊眾大潰，殺千餘人，所棄鎧仗、牛馬藉藉山野不可計。

translations.literal: Dingfang had just rested the troops when he saw dust rising; he led five hundred elite cavalry, crossed the ridge, and galloped to strike the enemy camp. The rebel masses routed in great disorder; more than a thousand were killed, and abandoned armor, weapons, cattle, and horses lay strewn over mountains and fields beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang had just let the men rest when he saw dust on the horizon. He led five hundred elite horsemen over the ridge in a dash on the enemy camp. The rebels broke in rout; more than a thousand were killed, and armor, weapons, cattle, and horses lay strewn across the hills beyond count.

sentences.zh: 副總管王文度疾其功，謬謂知節曰：「賊雖走，軍死傷者眾。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Wang Wendu, jealous of his achievement, falsely told Zhijie, "Though the rebels have fled, many in the army are dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Wang Wendu, jealous of his success, falsely told Zhijie, "The enemy may have fled, but our casualties are heavy.

sentences.zh: 今當結輜重陣間，被甲而趨，賊來即戰，是謂萬全。

translations.literal: Now we should array the baggage train in the midst of the formation, don armor and advance; if the enemy comes we fight at once—this is called complete security.
translations.idiomatic: We should march with the baggage train in the center of the formation, fully armored, and fight only when the enemy comes—that is the safe course.

sentences.zh: 」又矯制收軍不深入。

translations.literal: " He also forged an edict to recall the army and not advance deeply.
translations.idiomatic: " He also forged an order halting the advance.

sentences.zh: 於是馬癯卒勞，無鬥志。

translations.literal: Thereupon the horses grew thin, the soldiers weary, and there was no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The horses grew thin, the men exhausted, and fighting spirit collapsed.

sentences.zh: 定方説知節曰：「天子詔討賊，今反自守，何功之立哉？

translations.literal: Dingfang urged Zhijie, saying, "The Son of Heaven decreed a campaign against the rebels; now we turn instead to self-defense—how may achievement be established?
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang urged Zhijie, "The emperor ordered us to destroy the rebels. If we merely defend ourselves, what achievement can we claim?

sentences.zh: 且公爲大將，而閫外之事不得專，顧副將乃得專之，理不其然！

translations.literal: Moreover, you are the great commander, yet affairs beyond the pass may not be decided by you alone—only a deputy commander may decide them alone; is this not contrary to reason!
translations.idiomatic: You are the supreme commander, yet a deputy decides what happens beyond the frontier while you may not—that cannot be right!

sentences.zh: 胡不囚文度待天子命？

translations.literal: Why not imprison Wendu and await the Son of Heaven's command?
translations.idiomatic: Why not arrest Wendu and await the emperor's orders?

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " He did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhijie would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至怛篤城，有胡人降，文度猥曰：「師還而降，且爲賊，不如殺之，取其貲。

translations.literal: When they reached Tandu city, some Hu submitted; Wendu coarsely said, "They surrender only because the army is returning, and will yet become rebels—better kill them and take their goods.
translations.idiomatic: At Tandu city some non-Chinese submitted. Wendu said roughly, "They surrender only because we are turning back and will rebel again. Better kill them and seize their goods.

sentences.zh: 」定方曰：「此乃自作賊耳，寧曰伐叛！

translations.literal: " Dingfang said, "That would be making rebels of ourselves—how may one call it punishing rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: " Dingfang said, "That would make us the rebels ourselves. We came to punish rebellion!

sentences.zh: 」及分財，定方一不取。

translations.literal: " When goods were divided, Dingfang took not a single item.
translations.idiomatic: " When the spoils were divided, Dingfang took nothing.

sentences.zh: 高宗知之，比知節等還，悉下吏，當死，貸爲民。

translations.literal: Gaozong learned of it; when Zhijie and the others returned, all were sent down to the officials, sentenced to death, and their lives were spared only by reduction to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong learned of this and Zhijie and the others returned, all were arrested, condemned to death, and spared only by reduction to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 擢定方伊麗道行軍大總管，復徵賀魯，以任雅相、回紇婆潤爲副。

translations.literal: Dingfang was promoted to supreme commander on campaign of the Yili route and again campaigned against Helu, with Ren Yaxiang and the Uyghur Boporun as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang was made supreme commander on the Yili route and again marched against Helu, with Ren Yaxiang and the Uyghur Boporun as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 出金山北，先擊處木昆部，破之，俟斤嬾獨祿擁眾萬帳降，定方撫之，發其千騎並回紇萬人，進至曳咥河。

translations.literal: He went out north of the Golden Mountain, first struck the Chumukun tribe and defeated them; the yagbu Nandulu led his ten thousand tents in submission; Dingfang comforted them, sent out a thousand of their cavalry together with ten thousand Uyghurs, and advanced to the Yeqi River.
translations.idiomatic: Marching north of the Golden Mountain, he first defeated the Chumukun tribe. The yagbu Nandulu submitted with ten thousand tents. Dingfang won them over, took a thousand of their horsemen with ten thousand Uyghurs, and advanced to the Yeqi River.

sentences.zh: 賀魯率十姓兵十萬拒戰，輕定方兵少，舒左右翼包之。

translations.literal: Helu led a hundred thousand troops of the Ten Surnames to resist; he despised Dingfang's few soldiers and spread his left and right wings to envelop them.
translations.idiomatic: Helu met him with a hundred thousand warriors of the Ten Surnames, thinking Dingfang's force too small and spreading both wings to envelop him.

sentences.zh: 定方令步卒據高，攢槊外向，親引勁騎陣北原。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered the infantry to hold the heights, mass spears pointing outward, and personally led elite cavalry to form on the northern plain.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang posted his infantry on high ground with spears leveled outward and personally led his best cavalry onto the plain to the north.

sentences.zh: 賊三突步陣，不能入，定方因其亂擊之，鏖戰三十里，斬首數萬級，賊大奔。

translations.literal: The enemy thrice charged the infantry formation but could not enter; Dingfang struck them in their disorder, fought fiercely for thirty li, beheaded several tens of thousands, and the rebels fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy charged the infantry line three times without breaking through. Dingfang struck them in the confusion, fought for thirty li, took tens of thousands of heads, and put the enemy to rout.

sentences.zh: 明日，振兵復進，五弩失畢舉眾降，賀魯獨與處木昆屈律啜數百騎西走。

translations.literal: The next day he rallied the army and advanced again; the five Nuoshi tribes all rose and submitted with their masses; Helu alone, with several hundred horsemen of the Chumukun Quelü tribe, fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he advanced again. The five Nuoshi tribes all submitted. Helu fled west with only a few hundred horsemen of the Chumukun Quelü tribe.

sentences.zh: 定方令副將蕭嗣業、回紇婆潤率雜虜兵趨邪羅斯川追北，定方與雅相領新附兵絶其後。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered deputy commanders Xiao Siye and the Uyghur Boporun to lead mixed tribal troops to hurry to the Yaluo River in pursuit northward; Dingfang with Yaxiang led newly submitted troops to cut off their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang sent deputies Xiao Siye and the Uyghur Boporun with tribal auxiliaries in pursuit along the Yaluo River while he and Yaxiang cut off the rear with newly submitted troops.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，吏請少休，定方曰：「虜恃雪，方止舍，謂我不能進，若縱使遠遁，則莫能擒。

translations.literal: It happened to snow heavily; the clerks requested a brief rest. Dingfang said, "The barbarians rely on the snow and have just halted, thinking we cannot advance; if we let them flee far away, then none can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell and his officers asked to rest. Dingfang said, "The enemy trusts the snow and thinks we cannot advance. If we let them escape far away we shall never take them.

sentences.zh: 」遂勒兵進至雙河，與彌射、步真合，距賀魯所百里，下令陣而行，薄金牙山。

translations.literal: " He then drove the army forward to Shuanghe, joined Mizhe and Buzhen, was a hundred li from where Helu was, ordered the army to march in formation, and pressed close to Golden Tooth Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed on to Shuanghe, joined Mizhe and Buzhen, came within a hundred li of Helu, ordered the army to advance in battle order, and closed on Golden Tooth Mountain.

sentences.zh: 方賀魯將畋，定方縱擊，破其牙下數萬人，悉歸所部。

translations.literal: Just as Helu was about to hunt, Dingfang loosed an attack, defeated the several tens of thousands under his royal tent, and all returned to their original commands.
translations.idiomatic: Helu was out hunting when Dingfang struck, routed the tens of thousands at his royal camp, and brought them all back under imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 賀魯走石國，彌射子元爽以兵與嗣業會，縛賀魯以還。

translations.literal: Helu fled to the Stone Kingdom; Mizhe's son Yuanshuang led troops to join Siye, bound Helu, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Helu fled to the kingdom of Shi. Mizhe's son Yuanshuang joined Siye, bound Helu, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 由是脩亭障，列蹊隧，定疆畛，問疾收胔，唐之州縣極西海矣。

translations.literal: Thereby they repaired border posts, laid out paths and passes, fixed boundary markers, inquired after the sick and gathered the dead; Tang prefectures and counties reached to the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: They repaired frontier posts, opened roads and passes, fixed boundaries, tended the sick and gathered the dead, and Tang administration reached to the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 高宗臨軒，定方戎服奉賀魯以獻。

translations.literal: Gaozong came to the hall steps; Dingfang in military dress presented Helu as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong received him at the palace steps as Dingfang, in armor, presented Helu as a captive.

sentences.zh: 策功拜左驍衛大將軍、邢國公，別封子慶節爲武邑縣公。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and Duke of Xing State; his son Qingjie was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and Duke of Xing, and his son Qingjie was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 會思結闕俟斤都曼先鎮諸胡，劫所部及疏勒、硃俱波、喝般陀三國復叛，詔定方還爲安撫大使。

translations.literal: It happened that Duman, yagbu of the Sinie tribe, who had earlier governed the various Hu, plundered his command and the three states of Shule, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo rebelled again; an edict ordered Dingfang to return as Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Duman, yagbu of the Sinie, who had once governed the western peoples, led his followers and the states of Shule, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo in rebellion. Dingfang was ordered back as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 率兵至葉葉水，而賊堞馬頭川。

translations.literal: He led troops to the Yeya River while the rebels fortified at Matou River.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army to the Yeya River while the rebels fortified at Matou River.

sentences.zh: 定方選精卒萬、騎三千襲之，晝夜馳三百里，至其所。

translations.literal: Dingfang selected ten thousand elite soldiers and three thousand cavalry to strike them, galloping day and night three hundred li to reach their position.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang chose ten thousand elite foot soldiers and three thousand horsemen, rode day and night three hundred li, and fell on them.

sentences.zh: 都曼驚，戰無素，遂大敗，走馬保城。

translations.literal: Duman was startled; the battle had no order, and he was greatly defeated; he fled on horseback to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Duman was taken by surprise, his men fought without discipline, and he was routed. He fled on horseback into his walled camp.

sentences.zh: 師進攻之，都曼計窮，遂面縛降。

translations.literal: The army advanced to attack; Duman's stratagems were exhausted, and he came forward bound to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed the siege until Duman, at his wits' end, came out with hands bound to surrender.

sentences.zh: 俘獻於乾陽殿，有司請論如法。

translations.literal: The captive was presented at Qianyang Hall; the responsible offices requested sentencing according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The captive was presented at Qianyang Hall, and the judicial offices asked that he be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 定方頓首請曰：「臣向諭陛下意，許以不死，願丐其命。

translations.literal: Dingfang bowed his head and requested, saying, "Your servant earlier conveyed Your Majesty's intent and promised he would not die; I beg to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang kowtowed and said, "I had already conveyed Your Majesty's promise that he would not die. I beg that his life be spared.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕爲卿全信。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I will preserve your faith for your sake.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "For your sake I will keep that promise intact.

sentences.zh: 」乃宥之。

translations.literal: " He then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " And he pardoned Duman.

sentences.zh: 蔥嶺以西遂定。

translations.literal: West of the Congling Range was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The lands west of the Pamirs were thus secured.

sentences.zh: 加食邢州鉅鹿三百戸，遷左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was granted an additional three hundred households at Julu in Xingzhou and was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He received an additional three hundred households at Julu in Xing Prefecture and was made General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 出爲神丘道大總管，率師討百濟。

translations.literal: He went out as supreme commander on the Shenqiu route and led troops to campaign against Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as supreme commander on the Shenqiu route to campaign against Baekje.

sentences.zh: 自城山濟海至熊津口，賊瀕江屯兵，定方出左涯，乘山而陣，與之戰，賊敗，死者數千。

translations.literal: From Chenshan he crossed the sea to Ungjin; the enemy massed troops along the river. Dingfang came out from the left bank, took the mountain to form his battle line, fought them, defeated them, and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: From Chenshan he crossed the sea to Ungjin, where the enemy lined the riverbank. Dingfang came out on the left flank, drew up on the heights, routed them, and left several thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 王師乘潮而上，舳艫銜尾進，鼓而噪，定方將步騎夾引，直趨真都城。

translations.literal: The imperial army rode the tide upstream; ships followed one another's sterns in advance, drumming and shouting. Dingfang led infantry and cavalry on both flanks in support and drove straight for the capital Sabi.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial fleet rode the tide upstream, ships stem to stern, drums and shouts rolling. Dingfang led foot and horse on both flanks straight for the capital at Sabi.

sentences.zh: 賊傾國來，酣戰，破之，殺虜萬人，乘勝入其郛，王義慈及太子隆北走。

translations.literal: The enemy brought the whole state to meet them; after fierce fighting he defeated them, killed and captured ten thousand, pressed the victory into their outer walls, and King Uija and Crown Prince Yung fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy met them with the whole kingdom, fought a bitter battle, and were broken. Ten thousand were killed or captured. Pressing the victory into the outer city, King Uija and Crown Prince Yung fled north.

sentences.zh: 定方進圍其城，義慈子泰自立爲王，率眾固守。

translations.literal: Dingfang advanced to besiege the city; Uija's son Tae declared himself king and led the masses in stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang besieged the city while Uija's son Tae declared himself king and held out with the remaining forces.

sentences.zh: 義慈之孫文思曰：「王與太子出，而叔豈得擅爲王？

translations.literal: Uija's grandson Mun-ui said, "The king and crown prince have gone out—how may an uncle presume to make himself king on his own?
translations.idiomatic: Uija's grandson Mun-ui said, "The king and crown prince have fled. How can an uncle make himself king?

sentences.zh: 若王師還，我父子安得全？

translations.literal: If the imperial army returns, how may my father and I be kept whole?
translations.idiomatic: If the Tang army withdraws, how will my father and I survive?

sentences.zh: 」遂率左右縋城下，人多從之，泰不能止。

translations.literal: " He then led his attendants down the wall by rope; many people followed, and Tae could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his followers down the wall by rope. Many followed, and Tae could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 定方使士登城，建唐旗幟。

translations.literal: Dingfang had soldiers ascend the walls and raise Tang banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang sent men onto the walls to raise the banners of Tang.

sentences.zh: 於是泰開門請命，其將禰植與義慈降，隆及諸城送款，百濟平，俘義慈、隆、泰等獻東都。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tae opened the gates and begged for orders; his general Miruk and Uija surrendered, Yung and the various cities sent pledges of allegiance, Baekje was pacified, and Uija, Yung, Tae, and others were captured and presented at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tae then opened the gates and submitted. His general Miruk surrendered with Uija, Yung and the other cities sent pledges of loyalty, Baekje was pacified, and Uija, Yung, Tae, and the rest were sent as captives to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 定方所滅三國，皆生執其王，賞賚珍寶不勝計，加慶節尚輦奉御。

translations.literal: Of the three states Dingfang destroyed, he took all their kings alive; rewards of precious objects were beyond counting, and Qingjie was additionally made Chief of the Imperial Carriage Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the three kingdoms Dingfang destroyed he took every king alive. Rewards of treasure were beyond count, and Qingjie was made chief of the imperial carriage service.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定方爲遼東道行軍大總管，俄徙平壤道。

translations.literal: Before long Dingfang was made supreme commander on campaign of the Liaodong route; soon he was transferred to the Pyongyang route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made supreme commander on the Liaodong route, then transferred to the Pyongyang route.

sentences.zh: 破高麗之眾於浿江，奪馬邑山爲營，遂圍平壤。

translations.literal: He defeated Goguryeo forces at the Pae River, seized Mayi Mountain as camp, and then besieged Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Goguryeo army at the Pae River, seized Mayi Mountain for his camp, and besieged Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，解圍還。

translations.literal: Heavy snow came; he lifted the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow forced him to lift the siege and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 拜涼州安集大使，以定吐蕃、吐谷渾。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacification and Settlement Commissioner of Liangzhou to settle the Tibetans and Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Pacification Commissioner of Liangzhou to settle relations with Tibet and Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he died at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 667 at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 帝悼之，責謂侍臣曰：「定方於國有功，當褒贈，若等不言，何邪？

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him and reproached the attendant ministers, saying, "Dingfang had merit for the state and should have been honored posthumously—why did you not speak?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and rebuked his ministers: "Dingfang served the state with distinction and deserved posthumous honors. Why did none of you speak?

sentences.zh: 」乃贈左驍衛大將軍、幽州都督，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: " He then posthumously granted him General-in-Chief of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and military governor of Youzhou; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then posthumously made him General-in-Chief of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and military governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: =薛仁貴=

translations.literal: = Xue Rengui =
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui

sentences.zh: 薛仁貴，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Xue Rengui was a native of Longmen in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui was from Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少貧賤，以田爲業。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and lowly, making his living from the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was poor and obscure, earning his living as a farmer.

sentences.zh: 將改葬其先，妻柳曰：「夫有高世之材，要須遇時乃發。

translations.literal: When he was about to reinter his ancestors, his wife Liu said: "A husband who possesses talent surpassing the age must wait until the times suit him before it can blossom.
translations.idiomatic: As he was preparing to rebury his forebears, his wife Liu said, "You have gifts that outshine your generation—you need only the right moment for them to flourish.

sentences.zh: 今天子自征遼東，求猛將，此難得之時，君盍圖功名以自顯？

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is personally campaigning in Liaodong and seeking fierce generals—this is a rare opportunity; why do you not pursue merit and fame to distinguish yourself?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is leading the campaign in Liaodong himself and searching for bold commanders. Such a moment does not come twice. Why not win honor and make your name known?

sentences.zh: 富貴還鄕，葬未晩。

translations.literal: When wealth and rank are achieved and you return home, burial will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Return home in wealth and high station—the dead can wait for their tomb.

sentences.zh: 」仁貴乃往見將軍張士貴應募。

translations.literal: " Rengui thereupon went to see General Zhang Shigui and volunteered for service.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui took her counsel and went to General Zhang Shigui to enlist.

sentences.zh: 至安地，會郎將劉君邛爲賊所圍，仁貴馳救之，斬賊將，系首馬鞍，賊皆懾伏，由是知名。

translations.literal: Reaching Andi, he encountered the Langjiang Liu Junqiong besieged by bandits; Rengui galloped to rescue him, beheaded the rebel commander, hung the head from his saddle, and the bandits all cowered in submission; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: At Andi he found Langjiang Liu Junqiong surrounded by enemy troops. Rengui rode to his relief, cut down the rebel leader, and tied the severed head to his saddle until every foe shrank back in terror. His fame dates from that day.

sentences.zh: 王師攻安市城，高麗莫離支遣將高延壽等率兵二十萬拒戰，倚山結屯，太宗命諸將分擊之。

translations.literal: The imperial army attacked Ancheng City; Yeon Gaesomun of Goguryeo sent Generals Gao Yanshou and others leading two hundred thousand troops to resist, encamping backed by the mountains; Taizong ordered the various generals to attack them separately.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces besieged Ancheng, Yeon Gaesomun of Goguryeo dispatched Gao Yanshou and others with two hundred thousand men to meet them, camping with the mountains at their backs. Emperor Taizong ordered his commanders to strike from several directions.

sentences.zh: 仁貴恃驍悍，欲立奇功，乃著白衣自標顯，持戟，腰鞬兩弓，呼而馳，所向披靡；

translations.literal: Rengui, relying on his fierceness and daring, wished to achieve an extraordinary feat; he therefore put on white clothes to mark himself conspicuously, grasped a halberd, girded two bows at his waist, shouted and charged, and wherever he went none could stand against him;
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his ferocity, Rengui meant to win an unheard-of victory. He donned white so all could see him, took up a halberd, slung two bows at his belt, and with a battle cry spurred forward—every line he hit gave way before him.

sentences.zh: 軍乘之，賊遂奔潰。

translations.literal: The army followed in his wake, and the bandits then fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The main force swept up behind him, and the enemy broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 帝望見，遣使馳問：「先鋒白衣者誰？

translations.literal: The Emperor saw him from afar and sent a messenger galloping to ask: "Who is the vanguard in white?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw it from afar and sent a mounted courier to ask, "Who is that white-clad man leading the charge?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「薛仁貴。

translations.literal: " He was told: "Xue Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "Xue Rengui.

sentences.zh: 」帝召見，嗟異，賜金帛、口馬甚眾，授遊擊將軍、雲泉府果毅，令北門長上。

translations.literal: " The Emperor summoned him, marveled, bestowed abundant gold, silk, and livestock, appointed him General of Guerrilla Warfare and Guoyi of Yunquan Fu, and ordered him to serve as Changshang at the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him in audience, expressed astonishment, and lavished gold, silk, and horses upon him. He was made General of Guerrilla Warfare and Guoyi of the Yunquan Guard, and assigned to permanent duty at the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 師還，帝謂曰：「朕舊將皆老，欲擢驍勇付閫外事，莫如卿者。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Emperor said to him: "My veteran generals are all old; I wish to promote a bold warrior and entrust him with affairs beyond the frontier—there is no one like you.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the emperor told him, "My old commanders are aging. I mean to raise up a fierce champion and give him charge of campaigns abroad—and no one suits that role better than you.

sentences.zh: 朕不喜得遼東，喜得皦將。

translations.literal: I am not pleased at gaining Liaodong; I am pleased at gaining a brilliant general.
translations.idiomatic: I do not rejoice over winning Liaodong—I rejoice over winning a shining general.

sentences.zh: 」遷右領軍中郎將。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Right Colonel of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Colonel of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸萬年宮，山水暴至，夜突玄武門，宿衛皆散走，仁貴曰：「當天子緩急，安可懼死？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong visited Wannian Palace; a torrent suddenly arrived, and at night burst through the Xuanwu Gate; the palace guards all scattered and fled; Rengui said: "When the Son of Heaven is in peril, how can one fear death?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong was staying at Wannian Palace, a flash flood struck and in the night burst through the Xuanwu Gate. The palace guards fled in every direction. Rengui cried, "When the emperor's life hangs in the balance, who may shrink from death?

sentences.zh: 」遂登門大呼，以警宮內，帝遽出乘高。

translations.literal: " He then mounted the gate and shouted loudly to alert those within the palace; the Emperor hurried out and climbed to higher ground.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the gate and shouted to rouse the palace. The emperor hastened out and scaled the heights.

sentences.zh: 俄而水入帝寢，帝曰：「賴卿以免，始知有忠臣也。

translations.literal: Before long water entered the Emperor's quarters; the Emperor said: "Thanks to you I escaped harm—I now know there are loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the flood reached the imperial bedchamber. The emperor said, "I owe my life to you. Now at last I know what a loyal servant is.

sentences.zh: 」賜以御馬。

translations.literal: " He was granted an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was given one of the emperor's own horses.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方討賀魯，仁貴上疏曰：「臣聞兵出無名，事故不成，明其爲賊，敵乃可服。

translations.literal: When Su Dingfang campaigned against Helu, Rengui submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that when troops march forth without just cause, affairs do not succeed; only when it is made clear who are the villains will the enemy submit.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Dingfang's campaign against Helu, Rengui memorialized the throne: "I have heard that armies sent forth without a righteous name cannot prevail. Only when the wicked are clearly marked out will the foe acknowledge defeat.

sentences.zh: 今泥熟不事賀魯，爲其所破，虜系妻子。

translations.literal: Now the Nishu do not serve Helu and were broken by him; the captives hold their wives and children in bondage.
translations.idiomatic: The Nishu tribes refuse Helu's rule and were crushed by him; their families are held captive.

sentences.zh: 王師有於賀魯部落轉得其家口者，宜悉取以還，厚加賚遣，使百姓知賀魯爲暴而陛下至德也。

translations.literal: Where the imperial army has recovered their kin from Helu's tribes, they should all be taken and returned, richly rewarded and sent home, so that the people may know Helu is violent while Your Majesty's virtue is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever our forces have recovered such families from Helu's camps, they should all be restored to their people with generous gifts. Let the folk learn that Helu is a tyrant and Your Majesty a ruler of supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之，遂還其家屬，泥熟請隨軍效死。

translations.literal: " The Emperor accepted this, returned their families, and the Nishu asked to follow the army and die in its service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan. Their families were sent home, and the Nishu begged to march with the army and die in its ranks.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，詔副程名振經略遼東，破高麗於貴端城，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, he was ordered to serve under Cheng Mingzhen in securing Liaodong; they defeated Goguryeo at Guiduan City and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In 658 he was appointed deputy to Cheng Mingzhen for operations in Liaodong. They routed Goguryeo at Guiduan City and counted three thousand enemy dead.

sentences.zh: 明年，與梁建方、契苾何力遇高麗大將溫沙多門，戰橫山，仁貴獨馳入，所射皆應弦仆。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Liang Jianfang and Qibi Heli he encountered the Goguryeo general Wen Shadumen and fought at Hengshan; Rengui charged in alone, and every arrow he loosed felled its target as the string sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with Liang Jianfang and Qibi Heli, he met the Goguryeo commander Wen Shadumen at Hengshan. Rengui galloped deep into the enemy alone—every shaft he let fly struck home.

sentences.zh: 又戰石城，有善射者，殺官軍十餘人，仁貴怒，單騎突擊，賊弓矢俱廢，遂生擒之。

translations.literal: Again at Shicheng there was a skilled archer who killed more than ten officers and soldiers; Rengui grew angry, charged alone, the bandits' bows and arrows were all rendered useless, and he thereupon captured the man alive.
translations.idiomatic: At Shicheng an enemy marksman had killed more than a dozen imperial troops. Rengui, enraged, rode out alone. The man's bow failed him, and Rengui took him alive.

sentences.zh: 俄與辛文陵破契丹於黑山，執其王阿卜固獻東都。

translations.literal: Before long, together with Xin Wenling he defeated the Khitan at Heishan, seized their king Abu'gu, and presented him at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Xin Wenling smashed the Khitan at Black Mountain, captured their king Abu'gu, and brought him before the court at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 拜左武衛將軍，封河東縣男。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left Martial Guard and created Baron of Hedong County.

sentences.zh: 詔副鄭仁泰爲鐵勒道行軍總管。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as deputy to Zheng Rentai, Grand General on the Campaign of the Tiele Road.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed deputy to Zheng Rentai, commander of the Tiele campaign route.

sentences.zh: 將行，宴內殿，帝曰：「古善射有穿七劄者，卿試以五甲射焉。
