translations.literal: Before departing, he was feasted in the inner hall; the Emperor said: "In antiquity fine archers could pierce seven layers of felt; try shooting through five suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure the emperor entertained him in the inner hall. "Ancient masters pierced seven thicknesses of felt," he said. "Show me what you can do against five suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 」仁貴一發洞貫，帝大驚，更取堅甲賜之。

translations.literal: " With one shot Rengui pierced them completely through; the Emperor was greatly astonished and had stronger armor brought and granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: With a single arrow Rengui drove clean through them. The emperor, astonished, ordered heavier armor brought and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 時九姓眾十餘萬，令驍騎數十來挑戰，仁貴發三矢，輒殺三人，於是虜氣懾，皆降。

translations.literal: At that time the Nine Surname tribes numbered more than one hundred thousand; they sent several tens of elite horsemen to challenge battle; Rengui loosed three arrows and each time killed a man; thereupon the barbarians' spirit was cowed and all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Surname confederation mustered more than a hundred thousand men. They sent a few dozen of their fiercest riders to offer combat. Rengui fired three arrows and brought down three men. The enemy's courage broke, and they submitted.

sentences.zh: 仁貴慮爲後患，悉坑之。

translations.literal: Rengui feared they would become a later trouble and had them all buried alive in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they would rise again, Rengui had every one of them executed by burial alive.

sentences.zh: 轉討磧北餘眾，擒偽葉護兄弟三人以歸。

translations.literal: Turning to pursue the remaining forces north of the desert, he captured the three brothers of the false yabghu and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned against the remnants north of the desert and brought back the three brothers of the rebel yabghu.

sentences.zh: 軍中歌曰：「將軍三箭定天山，壯士長歌入漢關。

translations.literal: The army sang: "The general's three arrows settled the Heavenly Mountains; stout warriors sang their way through the passes into Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: A camp song ran: "Three arrows from the general settled the Tian Mountains; bold men marched home in triumph through the frontier passes of Han.

sentences.zh: 」九姓遂衰。

translations.literal: " The Nine Surname tribes then declined.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the Nine Surname confederation waned.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒有思結、多覽葛等部，先保天山，及仁泰至，懼而降，仁泰不納，虜其家以賞軍，賊相率遁去。

translations.literal: Among the Tiele were the tribes of Sijie, Dolangege, and others; they had first taken refuge on the Tian Mountains; when Rentai arrived they feared and surrendered, but Rentai did not accept them; he seized their families to reward the army, and the rebels fled one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele tribes of Sijie, Dolangege, and others had sheltered on the Tian Mountains. When Rentai arrived they submitted in fear, but he refused them. He took their families as booty to reward the troops, and the enemy bands slipped away in succession.

sentences.zh: 有候騎言：「虜輜重畜牧被野，可往取。

translations.literal: A scout reported: "The barbarians' baggage trains and herds cover the fields; we can go and take them.
translations.idiomatic: A patrol rider reported, "Enemy baggage and livestock cover the plain—we can ride out and seize them.

sentences.zh: 」仁泰選騎萬四千卷甲馳，絶大漠，至仙萼河，不見虜，糧盡還。

translations.literal: " Rentai selected fourteen thousand armored horsemen and galloped across the great desert to the Xian'e River; finding no enemy, they returned when provisions ran out.
translations.idiomatic: Rentai chose fourteen thousand armored riders and raced across the desert to the Xian'e River. They found no foe and turned back when their grain was spent.

sentences.zh: 人饑相食，比入塞，餘兵纔二十之一。

translations.literal: Men starved and ate one another; by the time they re-entered the passes, only one in twenty of the troops remained.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation drove them to cannibalism. By the time they reached the frontier, barely one soldier in twenty remained.

sentences.zh: 仁貴亦取所部爲妾，多納賕遣，爲有司劾奏，以功見原。

translations.literal: Rengui also took women from his command as concubines and accepted many bribes; he was impeached by the authorities but pardoned because of his merits.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui too had taken women from his ranks as concubines and accepted numerous bribes. Officials impeached him, but his past service won him pardon.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，高麗泉男生內附，遣將軍龐同善、高偘往慰納，弟男建率國人拒弗納，乃詔仁貴率師援送同善。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, Ch'ŏn Namsan of Goguryeo defected inward; the court sent Generals Pang Tongshan and Gao Kan to comfort and receive him; his brother Namgeon led the people of the state to refuse them; thereupon Rengui was ordered to lead troops to escort and support Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era, Ch'ŏn Namsan of Goguryeo came over to the Tang. The court sent Generals Pang Tongshan and Gao Kan to welcome him. His brother Namgeon rallied the kingdom to block them, and Rengui was ordered to march to Tongshan's aid.

sentences.zh: 至新城，夜爲虜襲，仁貴擊之，斬數百級。

translations.literal: Reaching Xincheng, they were attacked by the barbarians by night; Rengui struck them and beheaded several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Xincheng the enemy struck by night. Rengui counterattacked and took several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 同善進次金山，衄虜不敢前，高麗乘勝進，仁貴擊虜斷爲二，眾即潰，斬馘五千，拔南蘇、木底、蒼巖三城，遂會男生軍。

translations.literal: Tongshan advanced and halted at Jinshan; the barbarians were repulsed and dared not press forward; Goguryeo pressed the advantage, but Rengui struck the barbarians and cut them in two; the host at once collapsed; five thousand heads were taken; the three cities of Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan were seized; and he then joined Namsan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Tongshan pushed on to Jinshan, where the enemy was checked and held back. Goguryeo pressed the advantage, but Rengui split their force in two and the army broke at once. Five thousand heads were counted, the cities of Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan were taken, and he joined Namsan's force.

sentences.zh: 手詔勞勉。

translations.literal: An imperial letter in the emperor's own hand commended and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a letter in his own hand to praise and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 仁貴負銳，提卒二千進攻扶餘城，諸將以兵寡勸止。

translations.literal: Rengui, confident in his elite troops, led two thousand men to attack Fuyu City; the generals, citing the small number of troops, urged him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting his crack troops, Rengui led two thousand men against Fuyu City. The other commanders, citing their small numbers, urged him to hold back.

sentences.zh: 仁貴曰：「在善用，不在眾。

translations.literal: Rengui said: "Victory lies in skillful use, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui replied, "Victory depends on how troops are used, not on how many there are.

sentences.zh: 」身帥士，遇賊輒破，殺萬餘人，拔其城，因旁海略地，與李勣軍合。

translations.literal: " He personally led the soldiers; wherever they met the enemy they broke them, killed more than ten thousand, took the city, and then along the coast seized territory, joining Li Ji's army.
translations.idiomatic: He led the men himself. Every clash ended in victory. More than ten thousand were killed, the city fell, and he swept the coast before linking up with Li Ji's army.

sentences.zh: 扶餘既降，它四十城相率送款，威震遼海。

translations.literal: Once Fuyu surrendered, forty other cities submitted one after another; his authority shook the Liaohai region.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuyu submitted, forty other cities followed suit. His fame thundered across the Liaohai coast.

sentences.zh: 有詔仁貴率兵二萬與劉仁軌鎮平壤，拜本衛大將軍，封平陽郡公，檢校安東都護，移治新城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rengui to lead twenty thousand troops with Liu Ren'gui to garrison Pyongyang; he was appointed Grand General of his original guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang Commandery, made provisional Protector-General of Andong, and moved his headquarters to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed Rengui, with twenty thousand men, under Liu Ren'gui to garrison Pyongyang. He was made Grand General of his guard, created Duke of Pingyang, named provisional Protector-General of Andong, and moved his seat to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 撫孤存老，檢制盜賊，隨才任職，褒崇節義，高麗士眾皆欣然忘亡。

translations.literal: He comforted orphans and preserved the aged, restrained bandits and thieves, assigned offices according to talent, honored integrity and righteousness, and the scholars and commoners of Goguryeo all gladly forgot their state was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for orphans and the elderly, checked banditry, appointed men by merit, and honored loyalty and righteousness. The people of Goguryeo took heart and almost forgot their kingdom was gone.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，吐蕃入寇，命爲邏娑道行軍大總管，率將軍阿史那道真、郭待封擊之，以援吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, Tibet invaded; he was appointed Grand General on the Luosuo Campaign Road, leading Generals Ashina Daozhen and Guo Daifeng to strike them and relieve Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In 670 Tibet invaded. Rengui was made Grand General of the Luosuo campaign route and, with Generals Ashina Daozhen and Guo Daifeng, marched to strike the Tibetans and relieve Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 侍封嘗爲鄯城鎮守，與仁貴等夷，及是，恥居其下，頗違節度。

translations.literal: Daifeng had once been commander of Zhan City and was equal in rank with Rengui; now he was ashamed to serve under him and frequently disobeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng had once been garrison commander at Zhan City and had stood equal with Rengui. Now he resented serving beneath him and often defied his orders.

sentences.zh: 初，軍次大非川，將趨烏海，仁貴曰：「烏海地險而瘴，吾入死地，可謂危道，然速則有功，遲則敗。

translations.literal: At first the army halted at Danaichuan, about to press toward Wuhai; Rengui said: "Wuhai's terrain is perilous and malarial; we are entering a death zone—a truly dangerous path. Yet if we move fast there will be merit; if we delay, defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Danaichuan, bound for Wuhai, Rengui said, "Wuhai is treacherous ground, thick with miasma—we are marching into a death trap. Still, speed will bring victory; delay will bring ruin.

sentences.zh: 今大非嶺寬平，可置二柵，悉內輜重，留萬人守之，吾倍道掩賊不整，滅之矣。

translations.literal: The Danaichuan ridge is broad and level—we can set up two stockades, store all baggage within, leave ten thousand men to guard them, and we double our march to surprise the unprepared enemy and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: The Danaichuan ridge is broad and open. Set up two stockades there, put all baggage inside, leave ten thousand men to guard it, and we can double our march and catch the enemy unprepared.

sentences.zh: 」乃約賫，至河口，遇賊，破之，多所殺掠，獲牛羊萬計。

translations.literal: " They made their compact and pressed forward to the river mouth, encountered the enemy, defeated them, slaughtered and plundered extensively, and seized cattle and sheep numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed on the plan and pressed to the river mouth, where they routed the enemy, slaughtered and plundered freely, and took cattle and sheep by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 進至烏海城，以待後援。

translations.literal: They advanced to Wuhai City to await reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Wuhai City and waited for the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 待封初不從，領輜重踵進，吐蕃率眾二十萬邀擊取之，糧仗盡沒，待封保險。

translations.literal: Daifeng at first did not comply, followed with the baggage train, and Tibet led two hundred thousand men to intercept and seize it; provisions and weapons were entirely lost; Daifeng held a defensible position.
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng at first refused. He trailed behind with the baggage, and two hundred thousand Tibetans intercepted him. Provisions and arms were lost entirely, and Daifeng held a defensible position.

sentences.zh: 仁貴退軍大非川，吐蕃益兵四十萬來戰，王師大敗。

translations.literal: Rengui withdrew to Danaichuan; Tibet reinforced to four hundred thousand and came to battle; the imperial army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui fell back to Danaichuan. Tibet reinforced to four hundred thousand men and gave battle. The imperial army was routed.

sentences.zh: 仁貴與吐蕃將論欽陵約和，乃得還，吐谷渾遂沒。

translations.literal: Rengui made peace with the Tibetan general Lun Qinling and only then was able to return; Tuyuhun was thereupon lost.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui negotiated peace with the Tibetan general Lun Qinling and only then got his army out. Tuyuhun was lost.

sentences.zh: 仁貴嘆曰：「今歳在庚午，星在降婁，不應有事西方，鄧艾所以死於蜀，吾固知必敗。

translations.literal: Rengui sighed: "This year is gengwu, the stars are in Jianglou—it ought not to be a time for affairs in the west. This is why Deng Ai died in Shu; I knew from the start we must fail.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui sighed, "This is the year gengwu, with the stars in Jianglou—there should be no business in the west. Deng Ai died in Shu for just such a reason. I knew from the first we were doomed.

sentences.zh: 」有詔原死，除名爲庶人。

translations.literal: " An edict spared him from death and stripped his name, making him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared his life but stripped his rank and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 未幾，高麗餘眾叛，起爲雞林道總管。

translations.literal: Before long the remaining forces of Goguryeo rebelled; he was made Commander of the Jilin Road.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Goguryeo remnant forces rebelled, and he was raised up as Commander of the Jilin route.

sentences.zh: 復坐事貶象州，會赦還。

translations.literal: Again he was demoted to Xiang Prefecture for an offense; he was pardoned on an amnesty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was again demoted to Xiang Prefecture for another offense, then restored when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 帝思其功，乃召見曰：「疇歳萬年宮，微卿，我且爲魚。

translations.literal: The Emperor recalled his merits, summoned him, and said: "Years ago at Wannian Palace, but for you I would have become a fish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered his service and summoned him. "Years ago at Wannian Palace," he said, "but for you I would have drowned like a fish.

sentences.zh: 前日殄九姓，破高麗，爾功居多。

translations.literal: Recently in exterminating the Nine Surnames and breaking Goguryeo, your merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When you crushed the Nine Surnames and broke Goguryeo, no one did more than you.

sentences.zh: 人有言向在烏海城下縱虜不擊，以至失利，此朕所恨而疑也。

translations.literal: Some say that below Wuhai City you let the barbarians go without striking, and so the defeat came—that is what I resent and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that below Wuhai City you let the enemy go without striking, and that is why we lost. That is what I resent—and what I doubt.

sentences.zh: 今遼西不寧，瓜、沙路絶，卿安得高枕不爲朕指麾邪？

translations.literal: Now Liaoxi is unsettled and the roads to Guazhou and Shazhou are cut—how can you rest easy and not command for me?
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi is unsettled now, and the roads to Guazhou and Shazhou are cut. How can you sleep easy and refuse to fight for me?

sentences.zh: 於是拜瓜州長史、右領軍衛將軍、檢校代州都督，率兵擊突厥元珍於雲州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Prefect of Guazhou, General of the Right Imperial Guard, and provisional Governor of Daizhou, leading troops to strike the Turk Yuan Zhen at Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Prefect of Guazhou, General of the Right Imperial Guard, and provisional Governor of Daizhou, and sent to strike the Turk Yuan Zhen at Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥問曰：「唐將爲誰？

translations.literal: The Turks asked: "Who is the Tang general?
translations.idiomatic: The Turks asked, "Who commands the Tang army?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「薛仁貴。

translations.literal: " They were told: "Xue Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "Xue Rengui.

sentences.zh: 」突厥曰：「吾聞薛將軍流象州死矣，安得復生？

translations.literal: " The Turks said: "We heard General Xue was exiled to Xiang Prefecture and died—how can he live again?
translations.idiomatic: The Turks said, "We heard General Xue was exiled to Xiang Prefecture and died there. How can he be alive again?

sentences.zh: 」仁貴脫兜鍪見之，突厥相視失色，下馬羅拜，稍稍遁去。

translations.literal: " Rengui removed his helmet and showed himself; the Turks looked at one another and turned pale, dismounted and bowed in obeisance, and gradually slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui removed his helmet and showed his face. The Turks stared at one another, paled, dismounted, and bowed low before drifting away.

sentences.zh: 仁貴因進擊，大破之，斬首萬級，獲生口三萬，牛馬稱是。

translations.literal: Rengui pressed the attack and routed them completely, beheading ten thousand, capturing thirty thousand alive, with cattle and horses in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui pressed the attack and routed them utterly. Ten thousand heads were taken, thirty thousand captives seized, and cattle and horses beyond count.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 683, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈左驍衛大將軍、幽州都督，官給輿，護喪還鄕里。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand General of the Left Martial Cavalry Guard and Governor of Youzhou; an official bier was provided and his coffin escorted home.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand General of the Left Martial Cavalry Guard and Governor of Youzhou. The state provided a funeral carriage and escorted his body home.

sentences.zh: 仁貴子 訥子訥，字慎言，起家城門郎，遷藍田令。

translations.literal: Rengui's son Ne, styled Shenyan, entered office as Gate Guard Officer and was promoted to Magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui's son Ne, styled Shenyan, began his career as a Gate Guard Officer and was promoted to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 富人倪氏訟息錢於肅政臺，中丞來俊臣受賕，發義倉粟數千斛償之。

translations.literal: A wealthy man of the Ni clan sued at the Suizheng Office over interest on a loan; the Censor-in-Chief Lai Junchen accepted a bribe and issued several thousand bushels of grain from the Public Granary to satisfy the claim.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy Ni clansman brought suit at the Suizheng Office over interest on a loan. Censor-in-Chief Lai Junchen took a bribe and ordered several thousand bushels from the Public Granary paid to settle the claim.

sentences.zh: 訥曰：「義倉本備水旱，安可絶眾人之仰私一家？

translations.literal: Ne said: "The Public Granary exists to prepare for flood and drought—how can it cut off the people's sustenance to favor one household?
translations.idiomatic: Ne said, "The Public Granary exists to guard against flood and drought. How can we cut off the people's food to enrich one family?

sentences.zh: 」報上不與。

translations.literal: " He reported upward and the grain was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the throne, and the grain was not issued.

sentences.zh: 會俊臣得罪，亦止。

translations.literal: When Junchen fell from power, the matter also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Junchen fell from power, the matter was dropped as well.

sentences.zh: 後突厥擾河北，武后以訥世將，詔攝左威衛將軍、安東道經略使。

translations.literal: Later the Turks harried Hebei; Empress Wu, because Ne came from a family of generals, ordered him to serve provisionally as General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner for the Eastern Campaign Road.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Turks raided Hebei, Empress Wu, noting Ne's lineage of generals, ordered him to serve provisionally as General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner for the Eastern Campaign route.

sentences.zh: 對同明殿，具言：「醜虜馮暴，以廬陵王藉言，今雖還東宮，議不堅信。

translations.literal: At Tongming Hall he stated in full: "The vile barbarians rely on violence and cite the Prince of Luling as pretext. Though he has now returned to the Eastern Palace, people do not fully believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongming Hall he explained in full: "The barbarians are brutal and cite the Prince of Luling as their pretext. Though he has returned to the Eastern Palace, the court still doubts his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若太子無動，賊不討而解。

translations.literal: If the Crown Prince is seen to be unmoved, the bandits will disperse without a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: If the Crown Prince is seen to stand firm, the raiders will melt away without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」後納其言。

translations.literal: " The Empress later adopted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later took his advice.

sentences.zh: 俄遷幽州都督、安東都護。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Youzhou and Protector-General of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Youzhou and Protector-General of Andong.

sentences.zh: 改并州長史，檢校左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Bingzhou and made provisional Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Prefect of Bingzhou and made provisional Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 訥久處邊，有戰功。

translations.literal: Ne long served on the frontier and had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ne had long served on the frontier and won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 開元初，玄宗講武新豐，詔訥爲左軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong held military exercises at Xinfeng and ordered Ne to command the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era, Emperor Xuanzong held military exercises at Xinfeng and appointed Ne commander of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 時諸部頗失序，唯訥與解琬軍不動。

translations.literal: At the time the various units were largely in disorder; only Ne and Jie Wan's armies held their formation.
translations.idiomatic: The other units fell into disorder, but Ne and Jie Wan kept their armies in perfect formation.

sentences.zh: 帝令輕騎召之，至軍門，不得入。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent light cavalry to summon them; they reached the camp gate but were not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent light cavalry to summon them, but when the riders reached the camp gate they were turned away.

sentences.zh: 禮成，尤見慰勞。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he was especially commended and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When the exercises ended, the emperor singled him out for praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹、奚、突厥連和，數入邊，訥建議請討，詔監門將軍杜賓客、定州刺史崔宣道與訥帥眾二萬出檀州。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan, Xi, and Turks joined forces and repeatedly crossed the border; Ne proposed a punitive campaign; Du Binke, General of the Gate Guards, and Cui Xuandao, Prefect of Dingzhou, were ordered to join Ne in leading twenty thousand men out from Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Khitan, Xi, and Turks allied and raided the frontier repeatedly. Ne urged a punitive campaign. Du Binke, General of the Gate Guards, and Cui Xuandao, Prefect of Dingzhou, were ordered to join him with twenty thousand men marching from Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賓各議「方暑，士負戈贏糧深討，慮恐無功」，姚元崇亦持不可，訥獨曰：「夏草薦茂，羔犢方息，不費饋饟因盜資，振國威靈，不可失也。

translations.literal: Binke and the others argued that "it is midsummer; soldiers bearing arms and carrying extra provisions on a deep campaign will likely achieve nothing"; Yao Yuanchong also held it impossible; Ne alone said: "Summer grass is lush, lambs and calves are at rest—we need not spend much on supply and can seize the raiders' stores. To display the nation's might—this chance must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Binke and the others argued that in midsummer, troops laden with arms and extra grain on a deep strike would likely fail. Yao Yuanchong agreed. Ne alone said, "Summer grass is thick, lambs and calves are resting—we need little supply and can live off the raiders' stores. To show the empire's might, this chance must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 」天子方欲誇威四夷，喜奇功，乃聽訥言，而授紫微黃門三品以重之。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven wished to display might to the four barbarians and delighted in extraordinary feats; he therefore heeded Ne's words and conferred on him Third Rank at the Ziwei and Huangmen to give weight to his authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to awe the four quarters and loved bold strokes of victory. He accepted Ne's plan and granted him Third Rank at the Ziwei and Huangmen to lend weight to his command.

sentences.zh: 師至灤河，與賊遇，諸將不如約，爲虜覆，盡亡其軍。

translations.literal: The army reached the Luan River and encountered the enemy; the generals did not keep their agreement and were overwhelmed by the barbarians; the entire force was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached the Luan River and met the enemy. The commanders failed to keep their plan, were overrun, and the whole force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 訥脫身走，而罪宣道及大將李思敬等八人，有詔斬以徇，獨賓客免，盡奪訥官爵。

translations.literal: Ne escaped with his life but Cui Xuandao and the great general Li Sijing and seven others were held accountable; an edict ordered them beheaded as warning; only Binke was spared; all of Ne's offices and ranks were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Ne escaped alive. Cui Xuandao, the great general Li Sijing, and six others were held accountable and beheaded by edict as a warning. Only Binke was spared. All of Ne's offices and titles were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 俄而吐蕃大酋坌達延、乞力徐等眾十萬寇臨洮，入蘭州，剽牧馬，詔訥白衣攝羽林將軍，爲隴右防禦使，與王晙擊之。

translations.literal: Soon the great Tibetan chieftains Ben Dayan, Qili Xu, and others with a hundred thousand men raided Lintao, entered Lan Prefecture, and drove off pasturing horses; Ne was ordered to serve in plain clothes as provisional General of the Feathered Forest and Defender of Longyou, joining Wang Jun to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the great Tibetan chieftains Ben Dayan and Qili Xu led a hundred thousand men against Lintao, entered Lan Prefecture, and drove off the pastured horses. Ne was ordered to serve in plain clothes as provisional General of the Feathered Forest and Defender of Longyou, and marched with Wang Jun to strike them.

sentences.zh: 追及賊，戰武階驛，犄角劫之，破其眾；

translations.literal: They overtook the enemy and fought at Wujie Post, attacking from converging angles and breaking their force;
translations.idiomatic: They overtook the enemy and fought at Wujie Post, attacking from two sides and breaking their force;

sentences.zh: 尾北至洮水，又戰長城堡，殺鹵數萬，擒其酋六指鄕彌洪，悉收所掠及仗械不貲。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to the Tao River, they fought again at Changcheng Fort, killed barbarians numbering in the tens of thousands, captured the chieftain Liuzhi Xiangmihong, and recovered all that had been plundered together with weapons and gear beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing north to the Tao River, they fought again at Changcheng Fort, killed tens of thousands of the enemy, captured the chieftain Liuzhi Xiangmihong, and recovered all the plunder together with weapons and gear beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲自將北伐，及訥大克，乃止行。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor wished to lead the northern campaign in person; when Ne won a great victory, he then stopped the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been planning to lead the northern campaign himself, but when Ne won a great victory, he abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 命紫微舍人倪若水即軍陟功狀，拜訥左羽林大將軍，復封平陽郡公，以子暢爲朝散大夫。

translations.literal: He ordered Palace Secretariat Attendant Ni Ruoshui to go to the army and record meritorious deeds; Ne was appointed General of the Left Feathered Forest, again enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang Commandery, and his son Chang was made Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Palace Secretariat Attendant Ni Ruoshui to the camp to register achievements. Ne was made General of the Left Feathered Forest, restored as Duke of Pingyang, and his son Chang was appointed Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 又授涼州鎮軍大總管，赤水、建康、河源邊州皆隸節度。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Grand General Pacifying the Army of Liang Prefecture; the frontier prefectures Chishui, Jiankang, and Heyuan all came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Grand General Pacifying the Army of Liang Prefecture, with the frontier prefectures Chishui, Jiankang, and Heyuan placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 俄爲朔方行軍大總管。

translations.literal: Soon he became Grand Commander on Campaign of the Shuofang route.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Grand Commander on Campaign of the Shuofang route.

sentences.zh: 久之，以老致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time, on account of age he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After many years he retired on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈太常卿，謚曰昭定。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two; posthumously he was given the title Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous name Zhaoding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two. He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies and given the posthumous name Zhaoding.

sentences.zh: 訥性沈勇寡言，其用兵，臨大敵益壯。

translations.literal: Ne's nature was deep and brave, and he spoke little; in his use of troops, facing a great enemy he grew all the bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was deep-spirited and brave, sparing of speech. In battle he grew bolder still when facing a formidable foe.

sentences.zh: 訥弟 楚玉弟楚玉，開元中爲范陽節度使，以不職廢。

translations.literal: Ne's younger brother Chuyu, in the Kaiyuan era served as military governor of Fanyang and was dismissed for failure in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's younger brother Chuyu served as military governor of Fanyang in the Kaiyuan era and was removed for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 生子嵩。

translations.literal: He had a son named Song.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Song.

sentences.zh: 楚玉子 嵩嵩生燕、薊間，氣豪邁，不肯事產利，以膂力騎射自將。

translations.literal: Chuyu's son Song was born in the region between Yan and Ji; his spirit was bold and expansive, he refused to pursue property and profit, and relied on physical strength and horsemanship and archery to lead himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyu's son Song was born in the Yan and Ji region. Bold and high-spirited, he scorned trade and profit and lived by his strength, horsemanship, and archery.

sentences.zh: 豫安祿山亂，晩爲史朝義守相州。

translations.literal: He took part in An Lushan's rebellion and later served Shi Chaoyi's defense of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He joined An Lushan's rebellion and later defended Xiang Prefecture for Shi Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩破朝義，長驅河朔，嵩震懼，迎拜軍門，懷恩釋之，奏爲檢校刑部尚書、相衛洺邢等州節度使。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en defeated Chaoyi and drove deep into Heshuo; Song was shaken with fear, went out to bow at the army gate, and Huai'en released him and memorialized that he be made Acting Minister of Justice and military governor of Xiang, Wei, Ming, Xing, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en defeated Chaoyi and swept through Heshuo, Song was terrified. He went out to submit at the camp gate, and Huai'en spared him and recommended him as Acting Minister of Justice and military governor of Xiang, Wei, Ming, Xing, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 方大亂後，人亦厭禍，嵩謹奉職，頗有治名。

translations.literal: Just after the great disorder, people also wearied of calamity; Song diligently performed his duties and gained a considerable reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the great rebellion, when the people had had their fill of disaster, Song served conscientiously and earned a name for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，封高平郡王，實封二百戸，號其軍爲昭義。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping Commandery with an actual fief of two hundred households, and his army was styled Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali era he was made Prince of Gaoping with a fief of two hundred households, and his army was named the Zhaoyi command.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校尚書右僕射，更封平陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died and was posthumously given the title Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year and was posthumously made Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 詔其弟㟧知留後事，累加檢校太子少師。

translations.literal: An edict made his younger brother Yi acting governor in his stead, and he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed his younger brother Yi to handle affairs in his stead, and Yi was repeatedly promoted to Acting Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年，爲其將裴誌清所逐，以兵歸田承嗣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was driven out by his general Pei Zhicheng and took his troops to join Tian Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his general Pei Zhicheng expelled him, and he took his troops over to Tian Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 㟧奔洺州。

translations.literal: Yi fled to Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 請入朝，降服待罪銀臺門，赦之。

translations.literal: He requested to enter court, wore mourning garments and awaited punishment at the Silver Terrace Gate, and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to come to court, appeared in mourning dress to await judgment at the Silver Terrace Gate, and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 乃分其地，以蒿族子擇爲相州刺史，雄衛州刺史，堅洺州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon his territory was divided; Song's clansman Ze was made prefect of Xiang, Xiong prefect of Wei, and Jian prefect of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His territory was then divided. Song's clansman Ze was made prefect of Xiang, Xiong prefect of Wei, and Jian prefect of Ming.

sentences.zh: 承嗣誘雄亂，不從，遣客刺殺之。

translations.literal: Chengsi tried to incite Xiong to rebel; he would not follow, so Chengsi sent an agent to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi tried to incite Xiong to rebel. When Xiong refused, Chengsi sent an assassin to kill him.

sentences.zh: 初，嵩好蹴踘，隱士劉鋼勸止曰：「爲樂甚眾，何必乘危邀晷刻歡？

translations.literal: At first Song loved cuju; the recluse Liu Gang urged him to stop, saying, "There are many pleasures—why must you seize danger to snatch a moment's joy?
translations.idiomatic: At first Song was fond of cuju. The recluse Liu Gang urged him to stop, saying, "There are many pleasures in life. Why risk yourself for a moment's sport?

sentences.zh: 」嵩悅，圖其形坐右。

translations.literal: " Song was pleased and had his likeness painted and placed at his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: " Song was pleased and had Liu's portrait painted and kept at his side.

sentences.zh: 嵩子平。

translations.literal: Song's son was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Song had a son, Ping.

sentences.zh: 嵩子 平平字坦途，年十二，爲磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Song's son Ping, styled Tantu, at age twelve became prefect of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song's son Ping, styled Tantu, became prefect of Ci Prefecture at the age of twelve.

sentences.zh: 父喪，軍吏以故事脅知留務，偽許之，已而讓㟧，夕以喪歸。

translations.literal: When his father died, army officers coerced him by precedent to take charge of affairs in the governor's absence; he falsely agreed, then yielded to Yi, and by evening returned home for the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, the army officers pressed him by precedent to take charge of affairs. He pretended to agree, then yielded to Yi and returned home that evening to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 累授右衛將軍，宿衛三十年。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed General of the Right Guard and served in palace guard duty for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Guard and served in palace guard duty for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜黃掌擢爲汝州刺史，治有風績。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Du Huangshang promoted him to prefect of Ru Prefecture, where his governance had force and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Du Huangshang promoted him to prefect of Ru Prefecture, where he governed with distinction.

sentences.zh: 王師討蔡，繇左龍武大將軍授鄭滑節度使，數戰有功。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Cai, from his post as General of the Left Dragon Martial he was appointed military governor of Zheng and Hua and fought several battles with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched against Cai, he was made military governor of Zheng and Hua from his post as General of the Left Dragon Martial and won merit in several battles.

sentences.zh: 始，河溢瓠子，東泛滑，距城才二里所。

translations.literal: At first the Yellow River overflowed at Huzi and spread east toward Hua, coming within only about two li of the city.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Yellow River burst its banks at Huzi and flooded east toward Hua, coming within two li of the city walls.

sentences.zh: 平按求故道出黎陽西南，因命其佐裴弘泰往請魏博節度使田弘正，弘正許之。

translations.literal: Ping investigated and traced the old course southwest of Liyang, then ordered his aide Pei Hongtai to go request permission from Tian Hongzheng, military governor of Weibo, and Hongzheng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ping traced the old channel southwest of Liyang and sent his aide Pei Hongtai to ask Weibo military governor Tian Hongzheng for permission. Hongzheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃籍民田所當者易以它地，疏道二十里，以釃水悍，還壖田七百頃於河南，自是滑人無患。

translations.literal: Thereupon he registered the civilian fields that would be affected and exchanged them for other land, dredged a channel twenty li, and because the river waters were fierce, returned seven hundred qing of embankment fields south of the river; from then on the people of Hua had no further trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He registered the fields that would be affected and compensated the owners with other land, dredged a channel twenty li long, and because the river remained fierce, restored seven hundred qing of embankment land south of the river. After that the people of Hua were free from further trouble.

sentences.zh: 入爲左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court service as General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復帥鄭滑。

translations.literal: Before long he again commanded Zheng and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again put in command of Zheng and Hua.

sentences.zh: 李師道平，詔分淄、青、齊、登、萊五州爲平盧軍，徙平爲節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was pacified, an edict divided the five prefectures Zi, Qing, Qi, Deng, and Lai into the Pinglu command and transferred Ping to be its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao was defeated, an edict divided Zi, Qing, Qi, Deng, and Lai into the Pinglu command and made Ping its military governor.

sentences.zh: 王庭湊圍牛元翼，棣州危，詔平出援。

translations.literal: Wang Tingcou besieged Niu Yuanyi and Di Prefecture was in peril; an edict ordered Ping to go to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tingcou besieged Niu Yuanyi and Di Prefecture was in danger, Ping was ordered to march to its relief.

sentences.zh: 平遣將李叔佐率兵二千往，刺史王稷饋餉陋狹，眾潰而歸，推突將馬士端爲帥，劫屯士萬人，薄州堞。

translations.literal: Ping sent his general Li Shuzuo with two thousand troops; Prefect Wang Ji supplied provisions that were crude and scant, the troops broke and returned, chose the vanguard soldier Ma Shiduan as commander, gathered ten thousand mutineers in camp, and pressed close to the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Ping sent his general Li Shuzuo with two thousand men. Prefect Wang Ji supplied provisions that were meager and poor, and the troops broke and fled. They chose the vanguard soldier Ma Shiduan as leader, rallied ten thousand mutineers, and pressed against the city walls.

sentences.zh: 城中兵寡，平悉公帑家貲募銳卒二千迎戰，以奇兵掩賊輜重，賊狼顧，遂大敗，降，餘黨平。

translations.literal: The garrison in the city was few; Ping spent all public funds and family wealth to recruit two thousand elite soldiers to meet the attack, sent a surprise force to strike the rebels' baggage train, the rebels looked back in fear like wolves, and were then greatly defeated; they surrendered and the remaining factions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With few troops in the city, Ping spent the public treasury and his own fortune to raise two thousand elite soldiers and met the enemy in battle. A flanking force struck the rebels' baggage train, and the rebels broke in panic. They surrendered, and the remaining mutineers were pacified.

sentences.zh: 引謀亂者二千人斬堂皇下，脅從皆縱還田里，威震一方。

translations.literal: He led two thousand plotters of rebellion and beheaded them beneath the main hall; those coerced into following were all released to return to their fields, and his authority shook the whole region.
translations.idiomatic: He executed two thousand ringleaders beneath the main hall and released those who had been coerced, sending them back to their farms. His authority shook the whole region.

sentences.zh: 詔遷檢校尚書右僕射，封魏國公。

translations.literal: An edict transferred him to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed him as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 在鎮六年，兵鎧完礪，徭賦均一。

translations.literal: During six years in command, armor and weapons were kept complete and sharp, and corvée and taxes were uniform.
translations.idiomatic: During six years in command he kept armor and weapons in perfect order and levies and taxes fair and uniform.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，入朝，民鄣路願留，數日得出。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli era he entered court; the people blocked the road wishing to keep him, and only after several days could he get through.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoli era he came to court. The people blocked the road begging him to stay, and several days passed before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 拜檢校司空、河中降隰節度使，復得隸晉、慈二州，益兵三千。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Minister of Works and military governor of Hezhong, Jiang, and Xi, again gained jurisdiction over Jin and Ci prefectures, and received three thousand additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Minister of Works and military governor of Hezhong, Jiang, and Xi, regained authority over Jin and Ci prefectures, and was given three thousand additional troops.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒，更封韓召拜太子太保。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Minister of Education, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Han, and summoned and appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Minister of Education, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Han, and appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以司徒致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty and was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 平子 從子從，字順之，以廕授左清道率府兵曹參軍，累遷汾州刺史，隄文谷、濾河二水，引溉公私田，汾人利之。

translations.literal: Ping's nephew Cong, styled Shunzhi, by inherited privilege was appointed Army Staff Officer of the Left Clear Way Guard Command; he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Fen Prefecture, built dikes on the Wen Valley and Lu Rivers, and led irrigation for public and private fields, to the benefit of the people of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's nephew Cong, styled Shunzhi, entered service by inherited privilege as Army Staff Officer of the Left Clear Way Guard Command and rose to prefect of Fen Prefecture. He built dikes on the Wen Valley and Lu Rivers and irrigated public and private fields, to the great benefit of the people of Fen.

sentences.zh: 徙濮州，儲粟二萬斛以備凶災。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pu Prefecture and stored twenty thousand hu of grain against famine and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Pu Prefecture, he stored twenty thousand hu of grain against famine.

sentences.zh: 於是山東大水，詔右司郎中趙傑爲賑恤使，傑表其才，擢將作監。

translations.literal: Thereupon there was great flooding in Shandong; an edict made Right Department Director Zhao Jie relief commissioner, and Jie memorialized his talent, whereupon he was promoted to Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong was struck by severe flooding, Zhao Jie of the Right Department was made relief commissioner. Jie recommended Cong's abilities, and Cong was promoted to Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 終左領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as Senior General of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Senior General of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: =程務挺=

translations.literal: = Cheng Wuting =
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting

sentences.zh: 程務挺，洺州平恩人。

translations.literal: Cheng Wuting was a native of Ping'en in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting was from Ping'en in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父名振，隋大業末，仕竇建德爲普樂令，盜不跡境。

translations.literal: His father Mingzhen, at the end of the Sui Daye era, served Dou Jiande as magistrate of Pule, and thieves did not leave tracks within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mingzhen served Dou Jiande as magistrate of Pule in the final years of the Sui. Under his rule thieves vanished from the district.

sentences.zh: 俄棄賊自歸，高祖詔授永寧令，使率兵經略河北，即夜襲鄴縣，俘男女千餘人以歸，去數舍，閱婦人方乳者九十餘人，還之，鄴人感其仁。

translations.literal: Soon he abandoned the rebels and returned of himself; Emperor Gaozu ordered him appointed magistrate of Yongning and sent him to lead troops in pacifying Hebei. That very night he raided Ye County, captured more than a thousand men and women and returned; after going several stops, he reviewed more than ninety women who were nursing infants and sent them back, and the people of Ye were moved by his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He soon abandoned the rebels and surrendered to Tang. Emperor Gaozu appointed him magistrate of Yongning and sent him to pacify Hebei. That same night he raided Ye County and brought back more than a thousand captives. Several stops later he found more than ninety nursing mothers among them and sent them home. The people of Ye were deeply moved by his kindness.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥陷洺州，名振與刺史陳君賓自拔歸，母妻爲賊所得。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita captured Ming Prefecture, Mingzhen and Prefect Chen Junbin broke out and returned on their own; his mother and wife were taken by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita captured Ming Prefecture, Mingzhen and Prefect Chen Junbin fought their way out to rejoin the Tang. His mother and wife were captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 名振率眾千餘，掠冀、貝、滄、瀛等州，邀擊糧道，悉毀賊水陸餉具。

translations.literal: Mingzhen led more than a thousand men, raided Ji, Bei, Cang, Ying, and other prefectures, intercepted supply routes, and destroyed all the rebels' provisions and equipment by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen led more than a thousand men in raids across Ji, Bei, Cang, Ying, and neighboring prefectures, cutting supply lines and destroying the rebels' provisions and transport by land and water.

sentences.zh: 黑闥怒，殺其母妻。

translations.literal: Heita was enraged and killed his mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Heita executed his mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 賊平，請手斬黑闥，以其首祭母。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he requested to personally behead Heita and use his head to sacrifice to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, he asked to behead Heita with his own hand and offer the head in sacrifice to his mother.

sentences.zh: 拜營州長史，封東平郡公，賜物二千段、黃金三百兩。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Administrator of Ying Prefecture, enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery, and granted two thousand bolts of goods and three hundred liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chief Administrator of Ying Prefecture and Duke of Dongping, and granted two thousand bolts of goods and three hundred liang of gold.

sentences.zh: 轉洺州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made prefect of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼東，召問方略，不合旨，帝勃然詰之，名振辯對益詳，帝意解，謂左右曰：「房玄齡常在朕前，見朕嗔餘人，色不能主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, he summoned Mingzhen to ask strategy; it did not accord with the emperor's intent, and the emperor angrily questioned him. Mingzhen argued back in ever greater detail, the emperor's mood eased, and he said to those beside him, "Fang Xuanling is always before me; when he sees me angry at others, he cannot keep control of his expression.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, he summoned Mingzhen to discuss strategy. The answers displeased him, and he questioned Mingzhen angrily. Mingzhen replied in ever greater detail until the emperor's mood softened. He said to those around him, "Fang Xuanling is always at my side, yet when he sees me angry at others he cannot hide his fear.

sentences.zh: 名振生平未識我，一旦誚讓，而辭吐不屈，奇士哉！

translations.literal: Mingzhen in his whole life never knew me, yet in a single day he answered my rebuke, and his words did not bend—what a remarkable man!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen had never met me before, yet when I rebuked him his words never faltered. What a remarkable man!

sentences.zh: 」拜右驍衛將軍，平壤道行軍總管。

translations.literal: " He was appointed General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard and Commander on Campaign of the Pyongyang route.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard and Commander on Campaign of the Pyongyang route.

sentences.zh: 攻沙卑城，破獨山陣，皆以少擊眾，號爲名將。

translations.literal: He attacked Shabei City and broke the Dushan formation; in each case he used the few to strike the many, and was styled a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: He took Shabei City and broke the Dushan formation, each time defeating larger forces with smaller ones, and was acclaimed as a famous general.

sentences.zh: 遷營州都督，兼東夷都護。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Ying Prefecture and concurrently Protector-General of the Eastern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Area Commander of Ying Prefecture and Protector-General of the Eastern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 擊高麗於貴端水，焚其新城。

translations.literal: He struck Goguryeo at Guiduan River and burned their new city.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Goguryeo at Guiduan River and burned their new city.

sentences.zh: 歷晉、蒲二州刺史，鏤方道總管。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Jin and Pu prefectures and as Commander of the Lufang route.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jin and Pu prefectures and as Commander of the Lufang route.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右衛大將軍，謚曰烈。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title General of the Right Guard, with the posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of the Right Guard, with the posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 務挺少從父征討，以勇力聞，拜右領軍衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Wuting from youth followed his father on campaigns and was known for courage and strength; he was appointed Captain of the Right Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting followed his father on campaign from youth and won fame for courage and strength. He was appointed Captain of the Right Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 破突厥六萬騎於雲州。

translations.literal: He defeated sixty thousand Turkic horsemen at Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Yun Prefecture he routed sixty thousand Turkic horsemen.

sentences.zh: 會偽可汗阿史那伏念叛，總管李文暕等三將以次奔敗。

translations.literal: It happened that the false khan Ashina Funian rebelled, and the three generals including Commander Li Wenliang were defeated in succession and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the false khan Ashina Funian rebelled, three commanders including Li Wenliang were defeated in turn and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔裴行儉討之，以務挺副，檢校豐州都督。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pei Xingjian to suppress him, with Wuting as deputy and Acting Area Commander of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian was ordered to suppress the rebellion, with Wuting as his deputy and Acting Area Commander of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時伏念屯金牙山，務挺與副總管唐玄表引兵赴之，伏念懼，乃間道降於行儉，故裴炎以爲非行儉功，遷務挺右武衛將軍，封平原郡公。

translations.literal: At the time Funian was encamped at Golden Tooth Mountain; Wuting and Vice Commander Tang Xuanbiao led troops toward him, Funian was afraid, and by a hidden route surrendered to Xingjian. Therefore Pei Yan held that the credit was not Xingjian's; Wuting was transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Funian was encamped at Golden Tooth Mountain. Wuting and Vice Commander Tang Xuanbiao marched against him, and Funian, afraid, surrendered by a hidden route to Xingjian. Pei Yan therefore argued that the credit belonged not to Xingjian but to Wuting, who was promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 綏州部落稽白鐵餘據城平叛，建偽號，署置百官，進攻綏德、大斌，殺官吏，火區舍。

translations.literal: The Suizhou tribesman Ji Baitieyu seized the city to rebel, established a false reign title, appointed officials, advanced to attack Suide and Dabin, killed officials, and burned dwellings in the districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Suizhou tribesman Ji Baitieyu seized a city and rebelled, proclaimed himself ruler, appointed officials, attacked Suide and Dabin, killed officials, and burned dwellings throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 詔務挺與夏州都督王方翼討之，務挺生擒白鐵餘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wuting and Area Commander of Xia Prefecture Wang Fangyi to suppress him; Wuting captured Baitieyu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting and Wang Fangyi, Area Commander of Xia Prefecture, were ordered to suppress the rebellion, and Wuting captured Baitieyu alive.

sentences.zh: 進左驍衛大將軍，檢校左羽林軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and Acting Commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and Acting Commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖初，與右領軍大將軍張虔勖等豫廢中宗、立豫王爲皇帝，累被褒賚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Sisheng era, together with Senior General of the Right Army Guard Zhang Qianxu and others he took part in deposing Emperor Zhongzong and establishing the Prince of Yu as emperor, and was repeatedly rewarded and granted gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Sisheng era he joined Senior General of the Right Army Guard Zhang Qianxu and others in deposing Emperor Zhongzong and enthroning the Prince of Yu. He was repeatedly rewarded for his role.

sentences.zh: 以左武衛大將軍爲單于道安撫大使，禦突厥。

translations.literal: As General of the Left Martial Guard he was made Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu route to defend against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: As General of the Left Martial Guard he was made Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu route to guard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 務挺善綏禦，士服其威愛，突厥憚之，不敢盜邊。

translations.literal: Wuting was skilled at pacification and defense; soldiers submitted to his authority and affection, the Turks feared him, and dared not raid the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting excelled at frontier pacification. His soldiers respected both his authority and his kindness, the Turks feared him, and border raids ceased.

sentences.zh: 裴炎下獄，務挺密表申治，又素與唐之奇、杜求仁善，或言務挺與炎及徐敬業潛相援結，後遣左鷹揚將軍裴紹業即軍中斬之，籍其家。

translations.literal: When Pei Yan was imprisoned, Wuting secretly memorialized in his defense; he had also long been on good terms with Tang Zhiqi and Du Qiuren. Some said Wuting was secretly in league with Yan and Xu Jingye; the empress dispatched General of the Left Hawkish Yang Pei Shaoye to the army to behead him and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yan was imprisoned, Wuting secretly memorialized in his defense. He had long been friendly with Tang Zhiqi and Du Qiuren, and some claimed he was secretly allied with Yan and Xu Jingye. The empress sent General of the Left Hawkish Yang Pei Shaoye to the camp to execute him and confiscate his property.

sentences.zh: 突厥聞務挺死，率相慶，爲立祠，每出師，輒禱焉。

translations.literal: When the Turks heard that Wuting was dead, they all rejoiced together, built a shrine for him, and whenever they marched out they prayed there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks heard of Wuting's death they celebrated together, built a shrine in his honor, and prayed there whenever they took the field.

sentences.zh: =王孝傑=

translations.literal: = Wang Xiaojie =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaojie

sentences.zh: 王孝傑，京兆新豐人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaojie was a native of Xinfeng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaojie was from Xinfeng in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少以軍功進。

translations.literal: In youth he advanced through military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early through military merit.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，劉審禮討吐蕃，孝傑以副總管戰大非川，爲虜執，贊普見之，曰「貌類吾父」，故不死，歸之。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era, Liu Shenli campaigned against the Tibetans; Xiaojie as vice commander fought at Dafei River, was captured by the enemy, the tsenpo saw him and said, "Your appearance resembles my father," and therefore he was not killed and was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era Liu Shenli campaigned against Tibet. Xiaojie fought as vice commander at Dafei River and was captured. The Tibetan emperor saw him and said, "You look like my father," and spared his life and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 武后時，爲右鷹揚衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu he was General of the Right Hawkish Yang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as General of the Right Hawkish Yang Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝傑居虜中久，悉其虛實。

translations.literal: Xiaojie dwelt long among the barbarians and knew their strengths and weaknesses thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Having lived long among the Tibetans, Xiaojie knew their strengths and weaknesses intimately.

sentences.zh: 長壽元年，爲武威道總管，與阿史那忠節討吐蕃，克龜茲、于闐、疏勒、碎葉等城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changshou he was Commander of the Wuwei route and, together with Ashina Zhongjie, campaigned against the Tibetans and captured the cities of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Suyab, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In 692 he was made Commander of the Wuwei route and, with Ashina Zhongjie, campaigned against Tibet and recaptured Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Suyab, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 武后曰：「貞觀中，西境在四鎮，其後不善守，棄之吐蕃。

translations.literal: Empress Wu said, "In the Zhenguan era the western frontier lay in the Four Garrisons; afterward it was poorly defended and abandoned to the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said, "In the Zhenguan era the western frontier was held by the Four Garrisons, but later they were poorly defended and lost to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 今故土盡復，孝傑功也。

translations.literal: Now the old territory has all been recovered—this is Xiaojie's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Now the old territory has been fully recovered. That is Xiaojie's achievement.

sentences.zh: 」乃遷左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " She then promoted him to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 進夏官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品，清源縣男。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of the Summer Office, Third Rank of the same rank as the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, and Baron of Qingyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Summer Office with Third Rank at court and made Baron of Qingyuan County.

sentences.zh: 證聖初，復爲朔方道總管，與吐蕃戰不利，免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengsheng era he again became Commander of the Shuofang route; he fought the Tibetans with unfavorable results and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengsheng era he was again made Commander of the Shuofang route, but after an unsuccessful battle with Tibet he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 會契丹李盡忠等叛，有詔起白衣爲清邊道總管，將兵十八萬討之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan Li Jinzhong and others rebelled; an edict raised him from plain clothes to Commander of the Qingbian route with an army of one hundred eighty thousand to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong and others rebelled, an edict recalled him from civilian life as Commander of the Qingbian route at the head of one hundred eighty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 軍至東硤石谷，與賊接。

translations.literal: The army reached East Xiashi Valley and engaged the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached East Xiashi Valley and met the enemy.

sentences.zh: 道隘虜眾，孝傑率銳兵先驅，出谷整陣，與賊戰，而後軍總管蘇宏暉以其軍退，援不至，爲虜所乘，軍潰，孝傑墮谷死，士相蹂且盡。

translations.literal: The road was narrow and the enemy numerous; Xiaojie led elite troops as vanguard, emerged from the valley and formed ranks, and fought the rebels, but Rear Commander Su Honghui withdrew with his army, relief did not arrive, the enemy took advantage, the army collapsed, Xiaojie fell into the valley and died, and the soldiers trampled one another until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: The pass was narrow and the enemy numerous. Xiaojie led elite troops as vanguard, marched out of the valley, formed ranks, and gave battle. But Rear Commander Su Honghui withdrew his forces, reinforcements never came, and the enemy seized the advantage. The army collapsed. Xiaojie fell into the valley and died, and the soldiers trampled one another until nearly all were lost.

sentences.zh: 初，進軍平州，白鼠晝入營屯伏。

translations.literal: At first, when the army advanced on Ping Prefecture, white rats by day entered the camp and lay hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the army marched on Ping Prefecture, white rats entered the camp in broad daylight and hid there.

sentences.zh: 皆謂「鼠坎精，胡象也，白質歸命，天亡之兆」。

translations.literal: All said, "The rat is the spirit of the kan trigram; it is the image of the barbarians. White substance submits to fate—it is an omen of Heaven's destruction."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "The rat is the spirit of the kan trigram and the image of the northern barbarians. White creatures submitting by day is an omen that Heaven will destroy them."

sentences.zh: 及戰，乃孝傑覆焉。

translations.literal: When battle came, it was Xiaojie who was overturned.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, the omen was fulfilled and Xiaojie was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 時張説以管記還白狀，後問之，説具陳：「孝傑乃心國家，敢深入，以少當眾，雖敗，功可録也。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yue, as recorder, returned to report the situation; the Empress later asked him, and Yue fully explained: "Xiaojie was loyal at heart to the state, dared to push deep, faced many with few; though defeated, his merit can be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Yue had returned as recorder to report what had happened. The Empress later questioned him, and Yue set it all forth: "Xiaojie was utterly loyal to the state. He dared to drive deep, matched many with few, and though he was defeated, his merit deserves to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 」乃贈夏官尚書、耿國公，以其子無擇爲朝散大夫。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she posthumously made him Minister of the Summer Office and Duke of Geng, and made his son Wuzhe Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: " She then posthumously appointed him Minister of the Summer Office and Duke of Geng, and made his son Wuzhe Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 遣使者斬宏暉，使未至而宏暉已立功，遂贖罪。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to execute Honghui; before the envoy arrived Honghui had already achieved merit, and so his crime was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was dispatched to execute Honghui, but before the envoy arrived Honghui had already won distinction in battle, and his punishment was therefore remitted.

sentences.zh: =唐璿=

translations.literal: = Tang Xuan =
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing

sentences.zh: 唐璿，字休璟，以字行，京兆始平人。

translations.literal: Tang Xuan, courtesy name Xiujing, known by his courtesy name, was a man of Shiping in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing, courtesy name Xiujing, styled himself by his courtesy name. He was from Shiping in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖規，爲後周驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gui served as Grand General of Cavalry in Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui had served as Grand General of Cavalry under the Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 休璟少孤，授《易》於馬嘉運，傳《禮》於賈公彥，舉明經高第。

translations.literal: Xiujing was orphaned young; he studied the Changes under Ma Jiayun and the Rites under Jia Gongyan, and passed the Mingjing examination with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujing lost his father while still young. He studied the Book of Changes under Ma Jiayun and the Rites under Jia Gongyan, and passed the Mingjing examination with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 爲呉王府典簽，改營州戸曹參軍。

translations.literal: He served as Recorder of the Prince of Wu's household, then became Assistant Magistrate for Households in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder in the household of the Prince of Wu, then was transferred to Assistant Magistrate for Households in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會突厥誘奚、契丹叛，都督周道務以兵授休璟，破之於獨護山，數馘多，遷朔州長史。

translations.literal: When the Turks incited the Xi and Khitan to rebel, Area Commander Zhou Daowu entrusted troops to Xiujing, who defeated them at Mount Duhu; he took many heads and was promoted to Chief Administrator of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks incited the Xi and Khitan to rebel, Area Commander Zhou Daowu gave Xiujing command of troops, and he defeated them at Mount Duhu. He took many heads and was promoted to Chief Administrator of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，突厥圍豐州，都督崔智辯戰死，朝廷議棄豐保靈、夏。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era the Turks besieged Feng Prefecture; Area Commander Cui Zhibian died in battle, and the court debated abandoning Feng to hold Ling and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun era the Turks besieged Feng Prefecture. Area Commander Cui Zhibian fell in battle, and the court debated abandoning Feng and holding only Ling and Xia.

sentences.zh: 休璟以爲不可，上疏曰：「豐州控河遏寇，號爲襟帶，自秦、漢以來，常郡縣之。

translations.literal: Xiujing thought this impossible and memorialized: "Feng Prefecture controls the river and blocks raiders; it is called the collar and belt of the frontier. Since Qin and Han it has regularly been made a commandery and county.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujing held that this must not be done and memorialized: "Feng Prefecture commands the river and blocks invaders. It is called the collar and belt of the frontier. Since Qin and Han it has regularly been administered as commandery and county.

sentences.zh: 土田良美，宜耕牧。

translations.literal: The land and fields are fine and fit for farming and pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: Its soil and fields are excellent and suited to farming and grazing.

sentences.zh: 隋季喪亂，不能堅守，乃遷就寧、慶，戎羯得以乘利而交侵，始以靈、夏爲邊。

translations.literal: In the chaos at the end of Sui it could not be firmly held, so they moved to Ning and Qing; the Rong and Jie were able to seize advantage and raid back and forth, and Ling and Xia became the border.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, in the turmoil of collapse, it could not be held firm, so the seat was moved to Ning and Qing. The Rong and Jie were then able to exploit the opening and raid one another, and Ling and Xia became the frontier.

sentences.zh: 唐初，募人以實之，西北一隅得以完固。

translations.literal: Early in Tang they recruited people to fill it, and the northwest corner was thereby made secure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang, men were recruited to settle it, and the northwest corner was thereby made secure.

sentences.zh: 今而廢之，則河傍地復爲賊有，而靈、夏亦不足自安，非國家利也。

translations.literal: If it is abandoned now, the land along the river will again fall to the bandits, and Ling and Xia will not be secure themselves—it is not to the state's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: If it is abandoned now, the lands along the river will again fall to the enemy, and Ling and Xia will no longer be secure in themselves. That would not serve the state.

sentences.zh: 」高宗從其言。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozong accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，遷安西副都護。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era he was transferred to Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was transferred to Vice Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃破焉耆，安息道大總管韋待價等敗，休璟收其潰亡，以定西土，授靈州都督。

translations.literal: When Tibet destroyed Yanqi and Grand Commander Wei Daijia and others of the Anxi route were defeated, Xiujing gathered the scattered fugitives, stabilized the western lands, and was made Area Commander of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet destroyed Yanqi and Grand Commander Wei Daijia and others on the Anxi route were defeated, Xiujing gathered the scattered survivors, stabilized the western territories, and was appointed Area Commander of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乃陳方略，請復四鎮。

translations.literal: He then set forth strategy and requested recovery of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out a plan and petitioned for the recovery of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 武后遣王孝傑拔龜茲等城，自休璟倡之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu sent Wang Xiaojie to take Kucha and other cities—Xiujing had been the one to propose it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent Wang Xiaojie to recover Kucha and the other cities—an initiative that had begun with Xiujing.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，授涼州都督、右肅政御史大夫、持節隴右諸軍副大使。

translations.literal: In the Shenli era he was made Area Commander of Liang Prefecture, Right Censorate Grand Censor, and Vice Commissioner of the Longyou armies with plenipotentiary powers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenli era he was appointed Area Commander of Liang Prefecture, Right Censorate Grand Censor, and Vice Commissioner of the Longyou armies with plenipotentiary powers.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大將曲莽布支率騎數萬寇涼州，入洪源谷，休璟以兵數千臨高望之，見賊旗鎧鮮明，謂麾下曰：「吐蕃自欽陵死，贊婆降，莽布支新將兵，欲以示武，且其下皆貴臣酋豪子弟，騎雖精，不習戰，吾爲諸君取之。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Qu Mangbuzhi led tens of thousands of horsemen to raid Liang Prefecture and entered Hongyuan Valley. Xiujing with several thousand men looked down from high ground and saw the enemy flags and armor bright and fresh. He told his officers: "Since Qinling died and Zhanpo surrendered, Mangbuzhi has newly taken command and wishes to display martial prowess. Moreover his subordinates are all sons of noble ministers and tribal chiefs. Though their horses are fine, they are unused to battle. I will take them for you.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan general Qu Mangbuzhi led tens of thousands of horsemen against Liang Prefecture and entered Hongyuan Valley. Xiujing, with several thousand men, took the high ground and looked down on them. He saw the enemy banners and armor gleaming bright and said to his officers, "Since Qinling's death and Zhanpo's surrender, Mangbuzhi has newly taken command and means to show off his martial prowess. Moreover, those under him are all sons of great ministers and tribal chiefs. Their horses may be fine, but they are unused to battle. I will win them for you.

sentences.zh: 」乃被甲先登，六戰皆克，斬二將，獲首二千五百，築京觀而還。

translations.literal: " He then donned armor and led the ascent; six battles all won, two generals beheaded, 2,500 heads taken, a victory mound built, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He then donned armor and led the charge. Six battles, six victories. Two generals were beheaded and 2,500 heads taken. He built a victory mound and returned.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃來請和，既宴，使者屢覘休璟，後問焉，對曰：「洪源之戰，是將軍多殺臣士卒，其勇無比，今願識之。

translations.literal: Tibet came to sue for peace; after the banquet the envoy repeatedly observed Xiujing. The Empress later asked why, and the reply was: "At the battle of Hongyuan the general killed many of our soldiers; his bravery has no equal. We wish now to know him by sight.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet came to sue for peace. After the banquet the envoy kept studying Xiujing from afar. The Empress later asked why, and the reply was, "At the battle of Hongyuan that general killed many of our soldiers. His bravery has no equal. We wished now to know him by sight.

sentences.zh: 」後嗟異，擢爲右武威、金吾二衛大將軍。

translations.literal: " The Empress marveled and promoted him to Grand General of the Right Martial Wei Guard and the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress marveled and promoted him to Grand General of the Right Martial Wei and Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 西突厥烏質勒失諸蕃和，舉兵相攻，安西道閉。

translations.literal: The Western Turk Wuzhile lost harmony with the various frontier peoples and raised troops to attack one another; the Anxi route was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk Wuzhile fell out with the various frontier peoples and raised troops to attack one another, and the Anxi route was closed.

sentences.zh: 武后詔休璟與宰相計議，不少選，畫所當施行者。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Xiujing to confer with the chief ministers; he made no selections lightly and mapped out what should be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered Xiujing to consult with the chief ministers. He made no hasty choices and mapped out what should be carried out.

sentences.zh: 既而邊州建請屯置，盡如休璟策。

translations.literal: Soon the frontier prefectures submitted requests for garrison settlements, all exactly as Xiujing had planned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the frontier prefectures submitted plans for garrison settlements, all exactly as Xiujing had proposed.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「恨用卿晩。

translations.literal: The Empress said: "I regret employing you so late.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "I regret having used you so late.

sentences.zh: 」進拜夏官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Minister of the Summer Office and Third Rank of the same rank as the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Minister of the Summer Office with Third Rank at court.

sentences.zh: 後誚楊再思、李嶠、姚元崇等曰：「休璟諫知邊事，卿輩十不當一。

translations.literal: The Empress mocked Yang Zaisi, Li Jiao, Yao Yuanchong and others, saying: "Xiujing's counsel knows frontier affairs; not one of you ten equals him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress mocked Yang Zaisi, Li Jiao, Yao Yuanchong, and the others, saying, "When Xiujing advises on frontier affairs, not one of you is worth ten of him.

sentences.zh: 」改太子右庶子，仍知政事。

translations.literal: " He was made Right Vice Grand Master of the Heir Apparent but still handled affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Right Vice Grand Master of the Heir Apparent but continued to handle affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入塞，復以夏官尚書檢校幽營等州都督、安東都護。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the passes he was again made Minister of the Summer Office with acting authority as Area Commander of You, Ying and other prefectures and Protector-General of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided across the border, he was again made Minister of the Summer Office with acting authority as Area Commander of You, Ying, and other prefectures and Protector-General of Andong.

sentences.zh: 時中宗爲皇太子，休璟將行，進啟曰：「易之兄弟恩寵過幸，數入禁閫，非人臣所宜，願加防察。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongzong was crown prince. As Xiujing was about to depart he submitted a memorial: "The Zhang brothers' favor and grace exceed what is proper; they enter the forbidden inner quarters repeatedly—it is not what ministers should do. I beg that they be watched closely.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhongzong was crown prince. As Xiujing was about to depart, he submitted a memorial: "The Zhang brothers enjoy favor beyond what is proper. They enter the forbidden inner quarters again and again—conduct unbecoming a subject. I beg that they be watched closely.

sentences.zh: 」帝復位，召授輔國大將軍、同中書門下三品、酒泉郡公。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor was restored to the throne Xiujing was summoned and made Grand General Assisting the State, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor was restored to the throne, Xiujing was summoned and appointed Grand General Assisting the State, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「初欲召公計事，以有北狄憂，前日直言，今未忘也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At first I wished to summon you to discuss affairs, but there was worry over the northern barbarians. Your frank words the other day—I have not forgotten them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to him, "At first I wished to summon you to discuss affairs, but there was trouble with the northern barbarians. Your frank words the other day—I have not forgotten them.

sentences.zh: 」加特進、尚書右僕射，賜邑戸三百，封宋國公。

translations.literal: " He was given the special advance rank, made Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, granted three hundred fief households, and enfeoffed as Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: " He was granted special advance rank, made Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, given three hundred fief households, and enfeoffed as Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 是歳大水，上疏自劾免，不許。

translations.literal: That year there was severe flooding; he memorialized requesting his own dismissal and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year there was severe flooding. He memorialized asking to be dismissed and take the blame, but the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復起爲太子少師、同中書門下三品，監脩國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Junior Master of the Heir Apparent, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Superintendent of the compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Junior Master of the Heir Apparent, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Superintendent of the compilation of the National History.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，以特進爲朔方行軍大總管，備突厥；

translations.literal: Early in Jingyun he was made Grand Master with special standing and Grand Commander of the Shuofang field army to guard against the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun era he was made Grand Master with special standing and Grand Commander of the Shuofang field army to guard against the Turks;

sentences.zh: 停舊封，別賜百戸。

translations.literal: his old fief was suspended and he was separately granted one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: his old fief was suspended and he was separately granted one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明年，復請老，給一品全祿。

translations.literal: The next year he again requested retirement and was given full salary of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again asked to retire and was granted the full salary of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 延和元年卒，年八十六，贈荊州大都督，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanhe he died at eighty-six; posthumously made Grand Area Commander of Jing Prefecture, posthumous title Loyal.
