translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanhe he died at eighty-six. He was posthumously made Grand Area Commander of Jing Prefecture, with the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 休璟以儒者號知兵，自碣石逾四鎮，其間綿地幾萬里，山川夷坦，障塞之要，皆能言之，故行師料敵未嘗敗。

translations.literal: Xiujing, though a Confucian scholar, was renowned for military knowledge. From Jieshi to beyond the Four Garrisons, the continuous territory of nearly ten thousand li—mountains, rivers, level plains, and the vital points of barriers and passes—he could speak of them all. Therefore in campaigns and sizing up the enemy he never failed.
translations.idiomatic: Though a Confucian scholar, Xiujing was famed for knowing warfare. From Jieshi to beyond the Four Garrisons, across nearly ten thousand li of continuous territory—mountains and rivers, level plains, and the vital points of barriers and passes—he could speak of them all. Therefore in campaigns and in sizing up the enemy he never failed.

sentences.zh: 初得封，以賦絹數千散赒其族，又出財數十萬大爲塋墓，盡葬其五服親，當時稱重。

translations.literal: When he first received his fief he distributed several thousand bolts of silk tribute among his clan, and spent several hundred thousand in cash to build a great burial mound and bury all his relatives within five degrees of mourning; contemporaries praised his weight of character.
translations.idiomatic: When he first received his fief he distributed several thousand bolts of silk tribute among his clan, and spent several hundred thousand in cash to build a great tomb and bury all his relatives within the five degrees of mourning. Contemporaries praised his weight of character.

sentences.zh: 惟張仁愿議築受降城，而休璟獨謂不可，卒就之，而漠南無虜患。

translations.literal: Only when Zhang Renyuan proposed building the Accept Surrender cities did Xiujing alone say it could not be done; in the end it was done, and south of the desert there was no barbarian trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Zhang Renyuan proposed building the Accept Surrender cities did Xiujing alone say it should not be done. In the end the cities were built, and south of the desert there was no further trouble from the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 始老，已逾八十，猶托倚權近求復用。

translations.literal: When he first grew old, already past eighty, he still relied on those close to power to seek restoration to office.
translations.idiomatic: When he first grew old—already past eighty—he still leaned on those close to power in seeking to be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 於是賀婁尚宮方用事，附者輒榮赫，休璟乃爲子娶其義女，故復起宰相，頗爲時譏訾。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Attendant Helou was in power; those who attached themselves rose swiftly in glory. Xiujing had his son marry her adopted daughter, and so was recalled as chief minister—much criticized by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Palace Attendant Helou held power, and those who attached themselves to her rose swiftly in glory. Xiujing had his son marry her adopted daughter and was therefore recalled as chief minister—a move much criticized by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 其當國，亦無它毘益云。

translations.literal: When he held the state, he had no other benefit to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: When he held power, he brought no other benefit to speak of.

sentences.zh: 子先慎至陳州刺史，先擇爲右金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: His sons Xianshen reached Prefect of Chen and Xianze became General of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianshen rose to Prefect of Chen, and Xianze became General of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: =張仁愿=

translations.literal: = Zhang Renyuan =
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renyuan

sentences.zh: 張仁愿，華州下邽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Renyuan was from Xia Gui in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renyuan was from Xia Gui in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名仁亶，以睿宗諱音近避之。

translations.literal: His original name was Renyan; he changed it to avoid the taboo sound near Ruizong's name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Renyan; he changed it to avoid a sound too close to Ruizong's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 有文武材。

translations.literal: He had both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 武后時，累遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu he was successively promoted to Attendant Censor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was successively promoted to Attending Censor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 御史郭弘霸者，稱後乃彌勒佛身，又鳳閣舍人張嘉福、王慶之請以武承嗣爲皇太子，邀仁愿聯章，仁愿正色拒之。

translations.literal: The censor Guo Hongba claimed the Empress was the body of Maitreya Buddha; also Phoenix Pavilion Attendants Zhang Jiafu and Wang Qingzhi requested that Wu Chengsi be made crown prince—they invited Renyuan to join their memorial, but Renyuan sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Guo Hongba declared that the Empress was the earthly body of Maitreya Buddha. Phoenix Pavilion Attendants Zhang Jiafu and Wang Qingzhi also petitioned that Wu Chengsi be made crown prince and invited Renyuan to join their memorial. Renyuan sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 後王孝傑爲吐刺軍總管，與吐蕃戰不利，仁愿監其軍，因入言狀，孝傑坐免，擢仁愿侍御史。

translations.literal: Later Wang Xiaojie was Commander of the Tuci Army; he fought Tibet unfavorably. Renyuan supervised his army, entered court to report the situation, Xiaojie was dismissed, and Renyuan was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Xiaojie served as Commander of the Tuci Army and fought Tibet with poor results. Renyuan supervised his army, entered court to report what had happened, Xiaojie was dismissed, and Renyuan was promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 萬歳通天中，監察御史孫承景監清邊軍，戰還，自圖先鋒當矢石狀。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era Supervising Censor Sun Chengjing supervised the Qingbian Army; returning from battle he himself drew his position in the vanguard bearing arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era Supervising Censor Sun Chengjing supervised the Qingbian Army. Returning from battle, he himself drew a picture of himself in the vanguard facing arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 武后嘆曰：「御史乃能如是乎！

translations.literal: Empress Wu sighed and said: "Can a censor really be like this!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sighed and said, "Can a censor truly be like this!

sentences.zh: 」擢爲右肅政臺中丞，詔仁愿即敘其麾下功。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right Censorate; the Empress ordered Renyuan to immediately register the merit of those under his command.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengjing was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right Censorate, and the Empress ordered Renyuan to register at once the merit of those under his command.

sentences.zh: 仁愿先問承景破敵曲折，承景實不行，所問皆窮。

translations.literal: Renyuan first questioned Chengjing about the details of breaking the enemy; Chengjing had not actually gone and could not answer any question.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan first questioned Chengjing about the details of the victory over the enemy. Chengjing had not actually been there and could answer none of his questions.

sentences.zh: 仁愿劾奏承景罔上，虛列虜級。

translations.literal: Renyuan impeached Chengjing for deceiving the throne and fabricating enemy head counts.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan impeached Chengjing for deceiving the throne and fabricating enemy head counts.

sentences.zh: 貶爲崇仁令，以仁愿代爲中丞，檢校幽州都督。

translations.literal: Chengjing was demoted to Magistrate of Chongren; Renyuan replaced him as Censor-in-Chief and Acting Area Commander of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjing was demoted to Magistrate of Chongren. Renyuan replaced him as Censor-in-Chief and Acting Area Commander of You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 默啜寇趙、定，還出塞，仁愿以兵邀之，賊引去，矢著其手，武后遣使勞問，賜藥註傅。

translations.literal: Mochuo raided Zhao and Ding and withdrew beyond the passes; Renyuan intercepted with troops, the bandits withdrew, an arrow struck his hand; Empress Wu sent an envoy to comfort him and bestowed medicine and poultice.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo raided Zhao and Ding and withdrew beyond the passes. Renyuan intercepted him with troops, and the enemy withdrew, but an arrow struck his hand. Empress Wu sent an envoy to comfort him and bestowed medicine and poultice.

sentences.zh: 遷并州都督長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，進左屯衛大將軍，兼檢校洛州長史。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was promoted to Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guard and concurrently Acting Chief Administrator of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong era he was promoted to Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guard and concurrently Acting Chief Administrator of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會谷貴多盜，仁愿一切捕殺，胔積府門，畿甸震懾，無敢犯。

translations.literal: As grain was expensive and thieves numerous, Renyuan captured and killed them all; corpses piled at the prefectural gate; the capital region trembled in awe and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: As grain was costly and thieves numerous, Renyuan captured and killed them all. Corpses piled before the prefectural gate, the capital region trembled in awe, and none dared offend.

sentences.zh: 先是，賈敦頤嘗爲長史，有政績，時人爲之語曰：「洛有前賈后張，敵京兆三王。

translations.literal: Earlier Jia Dunyi had served as chief administrator with political achievements; people made a saying: "In Luo there is first Jia, later Zhang—they rival the three Wangs of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jia Dunyi had served as chief administrator with notable achievements, and people made a saying: "In Luo there is first Jia, then Zhang—they rival the three Wangs of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 三年，朔方軍總管沙咤忠義爲突厥所敗，詔仁愿攝御史大夫代之。

translations.literal: In the third year the Shuofang army commander Shatuo Zhongyi was defeated by the Turks; Renyuan was ordered as Acting Censor Grandee to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Shuofang army commander Shatuo Zhongyi was defeated by the Turks. Renyuan was ordered to serve as Acting Censor Grandee and replace him.

sentences.zh: 既至，賊已去，引兵踵擊，夜掩其營，破之。

translations.literal: When he arrived the bandits had already left; he led troops in pursuit, masked their camp by night, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the enemy had already withdrawn. He led troops in pursuit, struck their camp by night, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 始，朔方軍與突厥以河爲界，北崖有拂雲祠，突厥每犯邊，必先謁祠禱解，然後料兵度而南。

translations.literal: Initially the Shuofang army and the Turks took the river as boundary; on the north bank was the Fuyun Shrine; whenever the Turks raided the border they always first visited the shrine to pray and sacrifice, then assessed troops and crossed south.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Shuofang army and the Turks took the river as their boundary. On the north bank stood the Fuyun Shrine. Whenever the Turks raided the border they always first visited the shrine to pray and sacrifice, then mustered troops and crossed south.

sentences.zh: 時默啜悉兵西擊突騎施，仁愿請乘虛取漠南地，於河北築三受降城，絶虜南寇路。

translations.literal: At that time Mochuo had moved all his troops west to attack the Turgesh; Renyuan requested to seize the vacant land south of the desert and build three Accept Surrender cities north of the river, cutting off the barbarians' southern raid route.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mochuo had moved all his troops west to attack the Turgesh. Renyuan requested to seize the vacant lands south of the desert and build three Accept Surrender cities north of the river, cutting off the barbarians' southern route of invasion.

sentences.zh: 唐休璟以爲「兩漢以來皆北守河，今築城虜腹中，終爲所有」。

translations.literal: Tang Xiujing thought: "Since the two Han dynasties all have held north of the river; now building cities in the belly of the barbarians, in the end they will possess them."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing argued, "Since the two Han dynasties the frontier has been held on the north bank of the river. If we now build cities deep in barbarian territory, in the end they will fall into enemy hands."

sentences.zh: 仁愿固請，中宗從之。

translations.literal: Renyuan insisted; Zhongzong followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan pressed his case, and Zhongzong accepted it.

sentences.zh: 表留歳滿兵以助功，咸陽兵二百人逃歸，仁愿擒之，盡斬城下，軍中股栗，役者盡力，六旬而三城就。

translations.literal: He memorialized to retain troops whose term had expired to assist the work; two hundred Xianyang soldiers fled home; Renyuan captured them and beheaded them all below the wall; the army trembled in fear; the laborers exerted themselves fully; in sixty days the three cities were complete.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to retain troops whose terms had expired to assist the work. Two hundred soldiers from Xianyang fled home, but Renyuan captured them and beheaded them all below the wall. The army trembled with fear, the laborers exerted themselves to the utmost, and in sixty days the three cities were complete.

sentences.zh: 以拂雲爲中城，南直朔方，西城南直靈武，東城南直榆林，三壘相距各四百餘里，其北皆大磧也，斥地三百里而遠。

translations.literal: Fuyun was made the middle city, facing south straight toward Shuofang; the western city's south gate faced straight toward Lingwu, the eastern city's south gate toward Yulin; the three fortresses were each more than four hundred li apart; to their north was all great desert, extending territory three hundred li outward.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun became the middle city, facing due south toward Shuofang. The western city's south gate faced due south toward Lingwu, and the eastern city's south gate toward Yulin. The three fortresses stood more than four hundred li apart. To their north lay only great desert, extending the frontier three hundred li outward.

sentences.zh: 又於牛頭朝那山北置烽候千八百所。

translations.literal: Also north of Mount Niutou Chaona eight hundred beacon towers were established.
translations.idiomatic: North of Mount Niutou Chaona he also established eight hundred beacon towers.

sentences.zh: 自是突厥不敢逾山牧馬，朔方益無寇，歳損費億計，減鎮兵數萬。

translations.literal: From then on the Turks dared not cross the mountains to pasture horses; Shuofang was increasingly free of raiders; annual expenses decreased by hundreds of millions, and garrison troops were reduced by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Turks dared not cross the mountains to pasture their horses. Shuofang grew ever freer of raiders, annual expenses fell by hundreds of millions, and garrison troops were reduced by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 初建三城也，不置壅門、曲敵、戰格。

translations.literal: When the three cities were first built, no barrier gates, curved enemy screens, or battle frameworks were installed.
translations.idiomatic: When the three cities were first built, no barrier gates, curved enemy screens, or battle frameworks were installed.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「邊城無守備，可乎？

translations.literal: Someone said: "A frontier city without defenses—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "A frontier city without defenses—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」仁愿曰：「兵貴攻取，賤退守。

translations.literal: " Renyuan said: "In warfare offense is prized and retreat is despised.
translations.idiomatic: " Renyuan said, "In warfare offense is prized and retreat despised.

sentences.zh: 寇至，當並力出拒，敢回望城者斬，何事守備，退忸其心哉！

translations.literal: When bandits come, all forces should sally forth together to resist; whoever dares look back toward the city will be beheaded. Why install defenses? It would weaken their hearts for retreat!
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy comes, all forces should sally forth together to resist. Whoever dares look back toward the city will be beheaded. Why install defenses? That would only weaken their will to fight!

sentences.zh: 」後常元楷代爲總管，始築壅門，議者益重仁愿而輕元楷。

translations.literal: " Later Chang Yuankai replaced him as commander and first built barrier gates; commentators increasingly respected Renyuan and looked down on Yuankai.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Chang Yuankai replaced him as commander and was the first to build barrier gates. Commentators increasingly respected Renyuan and looked down on Yuankai.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，拜左衛大將軍、同中書門下三品，封韓國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong he was made Grand General of the Left Guard, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong he was made Grand General of the Left Guard, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 春還朝，秋復督軍備邊，帝爲賦詩祖道，賞賚不貲。

translations.literal: In spring he returned to court; in autumn he again directed troops to guard the frontier; the Emperor composed a farewell poem and bestowed rewards beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: In spring he returned to court; in autumn he again took command to guard the frontier. The Emperor composed a farewell poem for him and bestowed rewards beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Garrison Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand General of the Garrison Army.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，乃致仕。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended he retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, he retired.

sentences.zh: 加兵部尚書，稟祿全給。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Minister of War; full salary was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Minister of War, and his full salary was granted.

sentences.zh: 開元二年卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan he died; posthumously made Junior Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan he died and was posthumously made Junior Protector of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 仁愿爲將，號令嚴，將吏信伏，按邊撫師，賞罰必直功罪。

translations.literal: As a general Renyuan's orders were strict; officers and men trusted and obeyed him; on the frontier he comforted the armies; rewards and punishments matched merit and fault.
translations.idiomatic: As a general Renyuan's orders were strict, and officers and men trusted and obeyed him. On the frontier he comforted the armies, and rewards and punishments matched merit and fault.

sentences.zh: 後人思之，爲立祠受降城，出師輒享焉。

translations.literal: Later generations remembered him and built a shrine to him at Accept Surrender City; whenever troops marched out they would offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations remembered him and built a shrine to him at Accept Surrender City. Whenever troops marched out, they would offer sacrifice there.

sentences.zh: 宰相文武兼者，當時稱李靖、郭元振、唐休璟、仁愿云。

translations.literal: Of chief ministers who combined civil and military qualities, the age named Li Jing, Guo Yuanzhen, Tang Xiujing, and Renyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Of chief ministers who combined civil and military gifts, the age named Li Jing, Guo Yuanzhen, Tang Xiujing, and Renyuan.

sentences.zh: 在朔方，奏用御史張敬忠、何鸞、長安尉寇泚、鄠尉王易從、始平主簿劉體微分總軍事，太子文學柳彥昭爲管記，義烏尉晁良貞爲隨機，皆著稱，後至大官，世名仁愿知人。

translations.literal: At Shuofang he memorialized to employ Supervising Censor Zhang Jingzhong, He Luan, Chang'an Prefect Kou Ci, E Prefect Wang Yicong, and Shiping Assistant Magistrate Liu Tiwei to divide military affairs; Palace Scholar Liu Yanzhuo as recorder; Yiwu Prefect Chao Liangzhen as adjutant—all won renown and later reached high office; the world named Renyuan a knower of men.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuofang he memorialized to employ Supervising Censor Zhang Jingzhong, He Luan, Chang'an Prefect Kou Ci, E Prefect Wang Yicong, and Shiping Assistant Magistrate Liu Tiwei to divide military affairs; Palace Scholar Liu Yanzhuo as recorder; and Yiwu Prefect Chao Liangzhen as adjutant. All won renown and later reached high office, and the world named Renyuan a knower of men.

sentences.zh: 子之輔，至趙州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zhifu reached Prefect of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhifu rose to Prefect of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 張敬忠，自監察御史累遷吏部郎中，開元七年拜平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingzhong, from Supervising Censor was successively promoted to Bureau Director of Personnel; in the seventh year of Kaiyuan he was made Military Commissioner of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingzhong, starting from Supervising Censor, was successively promoted to Bureau Director of Personnel. In the seventh year of Kaiyuan he was made Military Commissioner of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: =王晙=

translations.literal: = Wang Jun =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun

sentences.zh: 王晙，滄州景城人，後徙洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was a man of Jingcheng in Cangzhou; later he moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was a native of Jingcheng in Cangzhou and later moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父行果，爲長安尉，知名。

translations.literal: His father Xingguo served as Warden of Chang'an and was well known.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingguo served as Warden of Chang'an and was well known.

sentences.zh: 晙少孤，好學。

translations.literal: Jun lost his father young and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lost his father while still young and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 祖有方奇之，曰：「是子當興吾宗。

translations.literal: His grandfather Youfang regarded him as remarkable and said: "This boy will revive our clan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Youfang thought him extraordinary and said, "This boy will revive our clan.

sentences.zh: 」長豪曠，不樂爲銜檢事。

translations.literal: " He grew bold and free-spirited and disliked work constrained by formal checks.
translations.idiomatic: " He grew bold and free-spirited and disliked work hemmed in by petty formalities.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，始調清苑尉，歷除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination, was first appointed Warden of Qingyuan, and was successively promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination, was first appointed Warden of Qingyuan, and was successively promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 會朔方元帥魏元忠討賊不利，劾奏副將韓思忠敗，律當誅。

translations.literal: When Shuofang Commander-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong's campaign against bandits went badly, he memorialized that deputy general Han Sizhong had been defeated and should by law be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuofang Commander-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong's campaign against bandits went badly, he memorialized that Deputy General Han Sizhong had been defeated and, by law, ought to be executed.

sentences.zh: 晙以「思忠偏裨，權不己制，且其人勇智可惜，不宜獨誅」，固爭，得釋，晙亦出爲渭南令。

translations.literal: Jun argued that "Sizhong was a subordinate officer whose authority was not under his own control, and his courage and wisdom were too valuable to waste—he should not be executed alone," protested fiercely, and secured his release; Jun was also transferred out to be Magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued that "Sizhong was a subordinate whose authority was not his own to command, and a man of such courage and wit was too valuable to lose—he should not die alone." After heated protest he secured Sizhong's release, but Jun himself was transferred out to serve as Magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，授桂州都督。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinglong he was appointed Military Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinglong era he was appointed Military Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 州有兵，舊常仰餉衡、永。

translations.literal: The prefecture had troops who had long depended on supplies from Heng and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture maintained troops who had long depended on grain shipped from Hengzhou and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 晙始築羅郛，罷戍卒；

translations.literal: Jun first built the outer wall of Luo and dismissed the garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: Jun first built the outer wall at Luo and dismissed the garrison troops;

sentences.zh: 埭江，開屯田數千頃，以息轉漕，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: dammed the river, opened thousands of qing of military colonies, thereby ending transported grain, and the people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: dammed the river, opened thousands of qing of military colonies, and thereby ended the need for transported grain; the people came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 後求歸上冢，州人詣闕留。

translations.literal: Later he asked to return home to tend his parents' tombs; the people of the prefecture went to the capital to petition that he stay.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to return home to tend his parents' tombs, and the people of the prefecture went to the capital to petition that he remain.

sentences.zh: 有詔：「桂往罹寇暴，戸口雕{疒齊}，宜即留，以須政成。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Guizhou has suffered bandit raids; the population is withered and depleted. He should remain at once and wait until his administration succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Guizhou has lately suffered bandit raids and its population is withered and depleted. He should remain at once and wait until his administration succeeds.

sentences.zh: 」在桂逾期年，人丐刻石頌德。

translations.literal: " He remained in Guizhou more than a year beyond his term; the people begged to carve stone in praise of his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " He remained in Guizhou more than a year beyond his term, and the people begged to carve stone in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 初，劉幽求放封州，廣州都督周利貞必欲殺之，道出晙所，晙知其故，留不遣。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Youqiu was exiled to Fengzhou; Guangzhou Commissioner Zhou Lizhen was determined to kill him. His route passed through Jun's jurisdiction; Jun knew the reason and detained him, refusing to send him on.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Youqiu was exiled to Fengzhou, and Guangzhou Commissioner Zhou Lizhen was determined to kill him. When his route passed through Jun's jurisdiction, Jun understood why and detained him, refusing to let him proceed.

sentences.zh: 利貞移書督趣，幽求懼曰：「勢且難全，正恐累君，奈何？

translations.literal: Lizhen sent letters pressing him; Youqiu feared and said: "The situation will be hard to survive; I fear I will implicate you—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen sent letters pressing him onward. Youqiu grew afraid and said, "The situation will be hard to survive, and I fear I will implicate you. What can be done?

sentences.zh: 」晙曰：「公之坐，非朋友所絶。

translations.literal: " Jun said: "Your offense is not one that friends should abandon you for.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun said, "Your offense is not one for which friends should abandon you.

sentences.zh: 晙在，終不忍公無罪就死。

translations.literal: While Jun lives, he cannot bear to see you die innocent.
translations.idiomatic: While I live, I cannot bear to see you die innocent.

sentences.zh: 俄崔湜等誅，幽求復執政，故詔幽求爲刻石辭。

translations.literal: Soon Cui Shi and others were executed; Youqiu returned to power, so Youqiu was ordered to compose the inscription for the stone monument.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cui Shi and others were executed, Youqiu returned to power, and Youqiu was ordered to compose the inscription for the stone monument.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚少卿，充朔方軍副大總管、安北大都護，豐安、安遠等城並授節度。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, appointed Deputy Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army and Grand Protector of Andong, with Feng'an, Anyuan, and other cities all placed under his military command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and appointed Deputy Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army and Grand Protector of Andong, with Feng'an, Anyuan, and other cities all placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 進太僕少卿、隴右群牧使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Stud and Commissioner of the Pasturelands of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Stud and Commissioner of the Pasturelands of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，吐蕃以精甲十萬寇臨洮，次大來谷，其酋坌達延以兵踵而前。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan Tibet sent a hundred thousand elite troops to raid Lintao, halting at Dalai Valley; their chieftain Banchi Dayan advanced with troops following close behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, Tibet sent a hundred thousand elite troops to raid Lintao and halted at Dalai Valley; their chieftain Banchi Dayan advanced with troops following close behind.

sentences.zh: 晙率所部二千與臨洮軍合，料奇兵七百，易胡服，夜襲，去賊五里，令曰：「前是寇，士大呼，鼓角應之。

translations.literal: Jun led his two thousand men to join the Lintao garrison, selected seven hundred elite troops, changed into barbarian dress, and attacked by night. Five li from the enemy he ordered: "When you reach the bandits, soldiers shout loudly and drums and horns answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led his two thousand men to join the Lintao garrison, selected seven hundred elite troops, changed into barbarian dress, and attacked by night. Five li from the enemy he ordered, "When you reach the bandits, shout loudly, and let drums and horns answer.

sentences.zh: 」賊驚，疑伏在旁，自相鬥死者萬計。

translations.literal: " The enemy panicked, suspecting ambush nearby, and killed each other in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy panicked, suspecting ambush nearby, and killed one another by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 俄而薛訥至武階，距大來二十里，賊陣兩軍間，互一舍而近。

translations.literal: Soon Xue Ne reached Wujie, twenty li from Dalai; the enemy camped between the two armies, each about one day's march away and close.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xue Ne reached Wujie, twenty li from Dalai. The enemy camped between the two armies, about one day's march from each and dangerously close.

sentences.zh: 晙往迎訥，夜使壯士銜枚鏖突，虜駭引去，追至洮水，敗之，俘獲如積。

translations.literal: Jun went to meet Ne; by night he sent strong men with gags in their mouths to charge fiercely; the barbarians fled in alarm; they pursued to the Tao River, defeated them, and captured booty heaped high.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went to meet Ne and, by night, sent strong men with gags in their mouths to charge fiercely. The barbarians fled in alarm; they pursued them to the Tao River, defeated them, and captured booty heaped high.

sentences.zh: 以功加銀青光祿大夫、清源縣男，兼原州都督；

translations.literal: For merit he was given the Silver Blue-Glittering Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made Baron of Qingyuan, concurrently Prefect of Yuanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was given the Silver Blue-Glittering Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made Baron of Qingyuan, concurrently serving as Prefect of Yuanzhou;

sentences.zh: 以子珽爲朝散大夫。

translations.literal: his son Ting was made Grand Master for Miscellaneous Uses.
translations.idiomatic: and his son Ting was made Grand Master for Miscellaneous Uses.

sentences.zh: 又進并州都督長史。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Chief Secretary to the Prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Chief Secretary to the Prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥默啜爲拔曳固所殺，其下多降，分置河曲。

translations.literal: The next year the Turk Mo-chuo was killed by the Bayegu; many of his followers surrendered and were distributed and settled in the bends of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Turk Mo-chuo was killed by the Bayegu; many of his followers surrendered and were distributed and settled along the bends of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 既而小殺繼降，降者稍稍叛去。

translations.literal: Soon after Xiao Sha also surrendered in succession; the surrendered people gradually rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Xiao Sha also surrendered in turn, and the surrendered people gradually rebelled and departed.

sentences.zh: 晙上言：

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 突厥向以國亂，故款塞，與部落無間也。

translations.literal: The Turks formerly, because their state was in turmoil, came in friendship to the frontier and were at peace with their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks formerly came in friendship to the frontier because their state was in turmoil, and they lived at peace with their tribes.

sentences.zh: 延素北風，何嘗忘之？

translations.literal: Their longing for the north wind—how could they ever forget it?
translations.idiomatic: Their longing for the north wind—how could they ever forget it?

sentences.zh: 今徙處河曲，使內伺邊罅，久必爲患。

translations.literal: Now resettled in the river bends, they can spy on frontier gaps from within; in time they will surely become a threat.
translations.idiomatic: Now resettled in the river bends, they can watch the frontier's weak points from within; in time they will surely become a threat.

sentences.zh: 比者不受要約，兵已屢動，擅作烽區，閉障行李。

translations.literal: Recently they have refused treaty terms; troops have already been mobilized repeatedly; they have set up beacon zones on their own and blocked frontier passes to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Recently they have refused treaty terms, troops have already been mobilized repeatedly, they have set up beacon zones on their own, and they have blocked frontier passes to travelers.

sentences.zh: 虜脫南牧，降帳必與連衡，以相應接，表裏有敵，雖韓、彭、孫、呉，無所就功。

translations.literal: If the barbarians break south to pasture, the surrendered camps will surely join in alliance to coordinate with them; with enemies inside and out, even Han Xin, Peng Yue, Sun Wu, and Wu Qi could achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If the barbarians break south to pasture, the surrendered camps will surely join in alliance and coordinate with them. With enemies inside and out, even Han Xin, Peng Yue, Sun Wu, and Wu Qi could achieve nothing.

sentences.zh: 請至農隙，令朔方軍大陳兵，召酋豪，告以禍福，啗以金繒，且言南方麋鹿魚米之饒，並遷置淮右、河南寬鄕，給之程糧。

translations.literal: I ask that at the farming interval the Shuofang army mass troops, summon tribal chiefs, explain fortune and disaster, entice them with gold and silk, and speak of the abundance of deer, fish, and rice in the south; resettle them all in broad townships south of the Huai and in Henan, providing them travel grain.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that at the farming interval the Shuofang army mass its troops, summon tribal chiefs, explain fortune and disaster, entice them with gold and silk, and speak of the abundance of deer, fish, and rice in the south. Resettle them all in broad townships south of the Huai and in Henan, and provide them travel grain.

sentences.zh: 雖一時之勞，然不二十年，漸服諸華，料以充兵，則皆勁卒。

translations.literal: Though it would be labor for a time, within twenty years they would gradually accept Chinese ways; assessed for military service, they would all become crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Though it would be labor for a time, within twenty years they would gradually accept Chinese ways, and if assessed for military service they would all become crack troops.

sentences.zh: 議者若謂降狄不可以南處，則高麗舊俘置沙漠之西，城傍編夷居青、徐之右，何獨降胡不可徙歟？

translations.literal: If critics say surrendered Di cannot be placed in the south, then former Goguryeo captives were placed west of the desert and barbarians from the city walls were settled east of Qing and Xu—why alone cannot the surrendered Turks be moved?
translations.idiomatic: If critics say surrendered Di cannot be placed in the south, then former Goguryeo captives were settled west of the desert and barbarians from the frontier cities were placed east of Qing and Xu. Why alone should the surrendered Turks not be moved?

sentences.zh: 臣復料議者必曰：「故事，置於河曲，前日已寧，今無獨異。

translations.literal: I further expect critics will say: "By precedent they were placed in the river bends; the frontier was already settled before; there is no need for a separate exception now.
translations.idiomatic: I further expect critics will say, "By precedent they were placed in the river bends; the frontier was already settled before, and there is no need for a separate exception now.

sentences.zh: 」且往者頡利破亡，邊鄙安定，故降戸得以久安。

translations.literal: " Moreover, in the past when Jieli was destroyed, the frontier was secure, so the surrendered households could live in long peace.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, in the past when Jieli was destroyed the frontier was secure, so the surrendered households could live in long peace.

sentences.zh: 今虜未殄滅，此降人皆戚屬，固不與往年同已。

translations.literal: Now the barbarians are not yet exterminated; these surrendered people are all kin of the enemy—they surely are not the same as in former years.
translations.idiomatic: Now the barbarians are not yet exterminated, and these surrendered people are all kin of the enemy—they surely are not the same as in former years.

sentences.zh: 臣請以三策料之：悉其部落置內地，獲精兵之實，閉黠虜之患，此上策也；

translations.literal: I ask to assess this with three strategies: move all their tribes into the interior—gain the substance of crack troops and shut out cunning barbarian trouble—this is the best strategy;
translations.idiomatic: I ask to assess this with three strategies: move all their tribes into the interior, gain the substance of crack troops, and shut out cunning barbarian trouble—this is the best strategy;

sentences.zh: 亭障之下，蕃華參處，廣屯戍，爲備擬，費甚人勞，下策也；

translations.literal: beneath the watchtowers, barbarians and Chinese mixed together, greatly expanding garrison colonies as a precaution—costly and laborious—this is the worst strategy;
translations.idiomatic: beneath the watchtowers, barbarians and Chinese mixed together, greatly expanding garrison colonies as a precaution—costly and laborious—this is the worst strategy;

sentences.zh: 置之胡塞，滋成禍萌，此無策也。

translations.literal: leave them in the barbarian frontier, nourishing the seeds of disaster—this is no strategy at all.
translations.idiomatic: leave them on the barbarian frontier, nourishing the seeds of disaster—this is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 不然，前至河冰，且必有變。

translations.literal: Otherwise, before the river freezes, there will surely be trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, before the river freezes there will surely be trouble.

sentences.zh: 書未報，而虜已叛，乃敕晙將并州兵濟河以討。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was answered, the barbarians had already rebelled; an edict ordered Jun to lead Bingzhou troops across the river to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial was answered, the barbarians had already rebelled, and an edict ordered Jun to lead Bingzhou troops across the river to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 晙間行，卷甲舍幕趨山谷，夜遇雪，恐失期，誓於神曰：「晙事君不以忠，不討有罪，天所殛者，當自蒙罰，士眾無罪。

translations.literal: Jun traveled by hidden routes, rolled up armor and abandoned tents to rush through valleys; at night they met snow; fearing to miss the deadline, he swore to the spirits: "If Jun serves his lord without loyalty and does not punish the guilty, let Heaven strike Jun alone—the troops are innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun traveled by hidden routes, rolled up his armor and abandoned his tents to rush through the valleys. At night they met snow, and fearing he would miss the deadline he swore to the spirits, "If Jun serves his lord without loyalty and does not punish the guilty, let Heaven strike me alone—the troops are innocent.

sentences.zh: 心誠忠，而天監之，則止雪反風，以獎成功。

translations.literal: If the heart is truly loyal and Heaven watches it, then let the snow stop and the wind reverse, to reward success.
translations.idiomatic: If the heart is truly loyal and Heaven watches it, then let the snow stop and the wind reverse to reward success.

sentences.zh: 」俄而和霽。

translations.literal: " Soon the weather cleared.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the weather cleared.

sentences.zh: 時叛胡分二道走，晙自東道追及之，獲級三千。

translations.literal: The rebel Turks fled in two directions; Jun pursued along the eastern route and caught them, taking three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Turks fled in two directions; Jun pursued along the eastern route, caught them, and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 以功遷左散騎常侍、朔方行軍大總管。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commander on Campaign in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was transferred to Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commander on Campaign in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 改御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 趯跌部及仆固都督勺磨等散保受降城之鄙，潛引突厥內擾，晙密言上，盡誘而誅之。

translations.literal: The Tuyue tribe and Pugu Governor Shaomo and others scattered to hold the outskirts of Accept Surrender City, secretly bringing Turks in to raid within; Jun secretly reported to the Emperor and lured them all in and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyue tribe and Pugu Governor Shaomo and others scattered to hold the outskirts of Accept Surrender City and secretly brought Turks in to raid within. Jun secretly reported to the Emperor, lured them all in, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 拜兵部尚書，復爲朔方軍大總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of War and again made Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of War and again made Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 九年，蘭池胡康待賓據長泉反，陷六州，詔郭知運與晙討平之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Lanzhou Hu Kang Daibin seized Changquan and rebelled, capturing six prefectures; an edict ordered Guo Zhiyun and Jun to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Lanzhou Hu Kang Daibin seized Changquan and rebelled, capturing six prefectures. An edict ordered Guo Zhiyun and Jun to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 封清源公，官一子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan and one son was given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan, and one son was given office.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以宮人賜知運等，晙獨不敢取，曰：「臣之事君，猶子事父，詎有常近圍掖而臣子敢當乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong bestowed palace women on Zhiyun and the others; Jun alone dared not accept and said: "In serving my lord I am like a son serving a father—how could a subject constantly near the inner quarters dare accept such a gift?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong bestowed palace women on Zhiyun and the others, but Jun alone dared not accept. He said, "In serving my lord I am like a son serving a father—how could a subject who constantly nears the inner quarters dare accept such a gift?

sentences.zh: 誓死以免。

translations.literal: I swear to die rather than accept.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than accept.

sentences.zh: 」見聽。

translations.literal: " His plea was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " His plea was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，晙奏：「朔方兵力有餘，願罷知運，獨當戍。

translations.literal: Earlier Jun had memorialized: "Shuofang's military strength is more than sufficient; I wish to dismiss Zhiyun and guard alone.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had memorialized, "Shuofang's military strength is more than sufficient; I wish to dismiss Zhiyun and guard the frontier alone.

sentences.zh: 」未報，而知運至，故不協。

translations.literal: " Before an answer came, Zhiyun arrived, so they did not cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: " Before an answer came, Zhiyun arrived, so they did not cooperate.

sentences.zh: 晙所降附，知運輒縱擊，賊意晙賣己，乃復叛。

translations.literal: Those whom Jun had surrendered, Zhiyun repeatedly let his men attack freely; the bandits thought Jun had sold them out and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Jun had persuaded to surrender, Zhiyun repeatedly let his men attack freely. The bandits thought Jun had sold them out and rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 晙坐貶梓州刺史。

translations.literal: Jun was demoted for the offense to Prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was demoted for the offense to Prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 改太了詹事、中山郡公。

translations.literal: He was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 進吏部尚書、太原尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel and Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel and Governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 代張説爲兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，充朔方軍節度大使，河北、河西、隴右、河東之軍盡屬。

translations.literal: Replacing Zhang Yue as Minister of War, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army; all armies of Hebei, Hexi, Longyou, and Hedong came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing Zhang Yue, he became Minister of War, Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army; all armies of Hebei, Hexi, Longyou, and Hedong came under his command.

sentences.zh: 是冬，帝親郊，追會大禮，晙以冰壯，請留將兵待邊，手敕慰勉。

translations.literal: That winter the Emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice; to meet the great rite Jun, citing thick ice, asked to remain with troops guarding the frontier; an autograph edict comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice. To meet the great rite Jun, citing thick ice, asked to remain with troops guarding the frontier, and an autograph edict comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 會有人告許州刺史王喬謀反，辭逮晙，詔源乾曜、張説雜訊，無狀，以黨與貶蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Wang Qiao, Prefect of Xuzhou, was plotting rebellion; the testimony implicated Jun; an edict ordered Yuan Qianyao and Zhang Yue to conduct a joint inquiry; no case was found, but he was demoted to Prefect of Qizhou as an associate.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Wang Qiao, Prefect of Xuzhou, was plotting rebellion, and the testimony implicated Jun. An edict ordered Yuan Qianyao and Zhang Yue to conduct a joint inquiry. No case was found, but he was demoted to Prefect of Qizhou as an associate.

sentences.zh: 遷定州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 復以戸部尚書爲朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was again made Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army with the title Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army with the title Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左丞相，謚曰忠烈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Left Grand Chancellor; posthumous title Loyal and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Grand Chancellor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: 晙氣貌偉特，時謂爲熊虎相。

translations.literal: Jun's bearing was exceptionally imposing; men of the time said he had the countenance of bear and tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's bearing was exceptionally imposing; men of the time said he had the countenance of bear and tiger.

sentences.zh: 感慕節義，有古人風。

translations.literal: He admired and pursued integrity and righteousness; he had the manners of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: He admired and pursued integrity and righteousness and had the manners of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 其操下肅壹，吏人畏愛。

translations.literal: In his conduct toward subordinates he was stern and orderly; officials and common people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: In his conduct toward subordinates he was stern and orderly, and officials and common people both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 始，二張之誣魏元忠，晙獨上疏申治。

translations.literal: When the Two Zhangs framed Wei Yuanzhong, Jun alone submitted a memorial to plead his case.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Zhangs framed Wei Yuanzhong, Jun alone submitted a memorial to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 宋璟曰：「魏公全矣，子再觸逆鱗，其殆乎！

translations.literal: Song Jing said: "Lord Wei is already safe—you touch the dragon's scales again; are you not in danger?
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing said, "Lord Wei is already safe—you touch the dragon's scales again. Are you not in danger?

sentences.zh: 」晙曰：「魏公以忠獲罪，茍得辨，雖死弗悔。

translations.literal: " Jun said: "Lord Wei was punished for loyalty; if I can vindicate him, I will not regret death.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun said, "Lord Wei was punished for loyalty. If I can vindicate him, I will not regret death.

sentences.zh: 晙卒後，信安王祎討奚於幽州，各捷，且言「戰時，士咸見晙與部將高昭麾兵赴敵」，天子嗟異。

translations.literal: After Jun died, Prince Xin'an Li Yi campaigned against the Xi in Youzhou with successive victories and reported: "In battle the soldiers all saw Jun and his subordinate general Gao Zhao waving troops to join the enemy." The Son of Heaven marveled.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun died, Prince Xin'an Li Yi campaigned against the Xi in Youzhou with successive victories and reported, "In battle the soldiers all saw Jun and his subordinate general Gao Zhao waving troops to join the fight." The Son of Heaven marveled.

sentences.zh: 戸部郎中陽伯成上疏，請封晙墓，表異之，優其子孫。

translations.literal: Bureau Director of Revenue Yang Bocheng submitted a memorial asking to ennoble Jun's tomb, mark him as extraordinary, and show favor to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director of Revenue Yang Bocheng submitted a memorial asking to ennoble Jun's tomb, mark him as extraordinary, and show favor to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣使祭晙廟，進諸子官。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent an envoy to sacrifice at Jun's shrine and promoted his sons in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent an envoy to sacrifice at Jun's shrine and promoted his sons in office.

sentences.zh: =史評=

translations.literal: = Historical Commentary =
translations.idiomatic: Historical Commentary

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「唐所以能威振夷荒、斥大封域者，亦有虎臣爲之牙距也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: "That Tang could awe the wild frontiers and expand its territory owed also to tiger ministers who served as fangs and claws.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says, "That Tang could awe the wild frontiers and expand its territory owed also to tiger ministers who served as fangs and claws.

sentences.zh: 至師行數千萬里，窮討殊鬥，獵取其國由鹿豕然，可謂選值其才歟！

translations.literal: Campaigns stretched tens of millions of li; they pursued enemies to exhaustion in desperate fighting and hunted their kingdoms as if they were deer and pigs—one may say the right men were chosen for the task!
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns stretched tens of millions of li; they pursued enemies to exhaustion in desperate fighting and hunted their kingdoms as if they were deer and pigs. One may say the right men were chosen for the task!

sentences.zh: 夫宰相代天秩物，燮化人神，惟有德者宜之。

translations.literal: A chief minister stands for Heaven in ordering all things and harmonizing men and spirits—only the virtuous are fit for this.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister stands for Heaven in ordering all things and harmonizing men and spirits—only the virtuous are fit for this.

sentences.zh: 若休璟、仁愿，用以丞弼，非強所不能邪？

translations.literal: If Xiujing and Renyuan were used as chief assistants—is that not forcing what cannot be forced?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiujing and Renyuan were used as chief assistants—is that not forcing what cannot be forced?

sentences.zh: 據功名之地，則綽綽矣。

translations.literal: Occupying the ground of merit and fame—they were more than adequate there.
translations.idiomatic: In the ground of merit and fame—they were more than adequate.
